drafts.ticket:
Lost phone for cloud sign-in

I just lost my work phone and can't sign in to the cloud console now. The multi-factor step keeps failing, even after trying to register on a new device. I registered the authenticator on my old phone, not a personal one. I need access to do my work, but the login is stuck here. I followed the help articles but they didn't work; my new phone isn't recognized. Can someone guide me on how to sign in properly with my new device?

claims.claim: Verify your identity through the standard process (manager confirmation plus employee ID).

cited.title: Lost phone for cloud console multi-factor sign-in
cited.text:
Lost phone for cloud console multi-factor sign-in (Identity, SSO and permissions)
## Symptom
The user has a new or lost phone and can no longer complete the multi-factor step when
signing in to the cloud console.

## Cause
Multi-factor for the console runs through the corporate identity provider. The
authenticator was registered on the old phone.

## Resolution steps
1. Verify the user's identity through the standard process (manager confirmation plus
   employee ID).
2. Ask the identity team to reset the user's multi-factor registration in the identity
   provider.
3. The user registers the authenticator on the new phone at the next sign-in.
4. If the phone was lost, ask the user to report it to security as a lost device.

## Warnings
Never turn multi-factor off for an account, even temporarily.

claims.claim: Ask the identity team to reset your multi-factor registration in the identity provider.

drafts.ticket:
Document creation blocked

Tried to create a material document but got 'Number range interval full' error. This happens with all document types: PO, SO, and accounting. Checked the system but can't find the interval manually. The error message is: EKKO000001 - Number range interval not found. Timestamp: 2026-04-15 10:30:00. Dependencies for next week's budget are stuck. Please help resolve this soon.

claims.claim: Note the exact error message and document type.

cited.title: Number range exhausted
cited.text:
Number range exhausted (Materials and number ranges)
## Symptom
Creating a document (material, purchase order, sales order or accounting document) fails
because no number can be assigned: the message says the number range interval is full or
was not found.

## Cause
Every document type draws its numbers from a number range interval. When the interval
reaches its upper limit, or the interval for a new fiscal year was never created, no new
documents of that type can be saved.

## Resolution steps
1. Note the exact message, the document type and the company code or plant.
2. Identify the number range object (for example FBN1 for accounting documents, MMNR for
   materials, or SNRO for the generic view).
3. Escalate to the SAP configuration team with the object, the interval and the fiscal
   year. Extending or adding an interval is a configuration change.
4. If the error appeared at the start of a fiscal year, mention it: the new year's
   interval may simply not have been created.

drafts.ticket:
Goods receipt blocked

Goods receipt in MIGO fails with blocked PO item error. Logged in as user1234, posting 1000 units of item A. Error code: R400001 - PO item blocked, cannot receive goods. Logs show issue occurred on 2026-02-15 14:30:00.

claims.claim: Display the PO in ME23N and open the item.

cited.title: Goods receipt fails because the PO item is blocked
cited.text:
Goods receipt fails because the PO item is blocked (Purchasing and goods receipt)
## Symptom
Posting a goods receipt in MIGO against a purchase order fails with a message that the
purchase order item is blocked, so the goods cannot be received.

## Cause
A buyer has blocked the PO item in ME22N (for example during a dispute with the
vendor), or the item has a deletion indicator. Blocked items cannot be received until a
buyer releases them.

## Resolution steps
1. Display the PO in ME23N and open the item. Check whether the item shows a block or a
   deletion indicator in the item overview.
2. Find the buyer from the PO header (purchasing group) and ask whether the block is
   intentional.
3. If the block should be removed, the buyer removes it in ME22N and saves the PO.
4. Retry the goods receipt in MIGO.
5. If the item has a deletion indicator and the goods have physically arrived, the buyer
   must create a new PO item; a deleted item cannot be received.

claims.claim: Check if the item shows a block or a deletion indicator in the item overview.

drafts.ticket:
Developer tool fails with certificate error

Every time I run the tool, it gives me a certificate error. It works fine at home, only issues here in the office network. Tried reinstalling the tool and updating certificates, no change. The error says 'unable to get local issuer certificate'. Other tools work, so it’s probably a configuration issue. Need this to meet the project deadline; blocking development.

claims.claim: Confirm the error appears only on the office network or VPN.

cited.title: Certificate errors in a desktop tool on the office network
cited.text:
Certificate errors in a desktop tool on the office network (Firewall and proxy)
## Symptom
A developer tool, command-line client or desktop app fails with an SSL or certificate
error ("unable to get local issuer certificate", "self-signed certificate in chain") on
the office network, but works at home.

## Cause
The web proxy inspects encrypted traffic and re-signs it with the company's root
certificate. Browsers trust that certificate, but some tools use their own certificate
store and do not.

## Resolution steps
1. Confirm the error appears only on the office network or VPN.
2. Point the tool at the company root certificate, which is published on the intranet
   (most tools have a setting or environment variable for a CA bundle).
3. If the tool cannot be configured, raise a request for an inspection bypass for that
   domain, with the business reason.

## Warnings
Never turn off certificate verification in the tool; it removes protection against
real interception.

drafts.ticket:
Missed timesheet deadline

Hi HR team, I missed the timesheet deadline this week. Can you confirm if it affects my payroll this month? Also, what are the consequences of missing a deadline? What are the consequences of missing a deadline for payroll processing this month if I submit late this week?

claims.claim: Submit your timesheet in the HR portal as soon as possible, even if late.

cited.title: Missed timesheet deadline
cited.text:
Missed timesheet deadline (Payroll and timesheets)
## Symptom
An employee or manager asks about the timesheet deadline or a missed submission.

## Cause
Timesheets are due every Friday by end of day and must be approved by the manager before
the payroll cut-off to be paid in that cycle.

## Resolution steps
1. Submit the timesheet in the HR portal even if late; late timesheets are accepted until
   the payroll cut-off.
2. Ask the manager to approve it before the cut-off.
3. After the cut-off, the hours are paid in the following cycle.
4. Contractors and hourly staff have an earlier cut-off; confirm the employment type
   before quoting a deadline.

## Warnings
Do not edit or approve a timesheet on an employee's or manager's behalf.

claims.claim: Ask your manager to approve it before the payroll cut-off.

drafts.ticket:
Internal network unreachable

Connected to VPN, but internal sites and SAP won't load. What's going wrong with DNS resolution? Is there a timeout for DNS resolution when connected to the VPN from home networks like mine?

claims.claim: Check if internal resources can be accessed by IP address.

cited.title: VPN connected but internal sites do not open
cited.text:
VPN connected but internal sites do not open (VPN connectivity)
## Symptom
The VPN client says it is connected, but internal websites, file shares and SAP do not
open. Public websites still work.

## Cause
The VPN tunnel is up but the laptop is not using the internal DNS servers pushed by the
VPN, or a home router uses the same private address range as an internal network, so
traffic for that range never enters the tunnel.

## Resolution steps
1. Ask the user to try an internal resource by IP address. If the IP works but the name
   does not, it is a DNS problem.
2. Run `ipconfig /all` and check that the VPN adapter lists the internal DNS servers.
3. Disconnect and reconnect the VPN; if DNS is still wrong, reinstall the VPN profile from
   the software centre.
4. If even IP addresses fail, compare the home network's address range with the internal
   ranges (for example both using 192.168.1.x). Ask the user to restart the home router
   or test from a hotspot, and report the overlap to network engineering.

cited.title: Internal names do not resolve
cited.text:
Internal names do not resolve (DHCP and DNS)
## Symptom
Public websites work, but internal names such as the intranet or a file server do not
open. The same resource opens when the user types its IP address.

## Cause
The device is not using the internal DNS servers: it is off the corporate network or VPN,
or it has public DNS servers set, which cannot resolve internal names.

## Resolution steps
1. Confirm the device is on the corporate network or connected to the VPN.
2. Run `ipconfig /all` and check that the DNS servers are the internal ones, not public
   resolvers such as 8.8.8.8.
3. If public DNS servers were set by hand, set the adapter back to obtain DNS
   automatically.
4. Run `ipconfig /flushdns` and retry.

## Warnings
Once the IP address works but the name does not, do not keep checking cables and Wi-Fi;
it is a DNS problem.

cited.title: Schema migration failed halfway
cited.text:
Schema migration failed halfway (Access requests and schema changes)
## Symptom
A schema migration failed during deployment, and it is unclear which changes were applied.

## Cause
Migrations that are not run in one transaction (for example with `CREATE INDEX
CONCURRENTLY`) can stop halfway. The migration tool's version table may not match what
was really applied.

## Resolution steps
1. Check the version table (for example `alembic_version`) to see what the tool recorded.
2. Compare the actual schema with what the migration should produce.
3. Finish or undo the partial change by hand so the schema matches one known version.
4. Then mark the version or rerun the migration, and record what was done in the ticket.

## Warnings
Never rerun a failed migration before you know which statements already applied.

cited.title: Connected but no internet, 169.254 address
cited.text:
Connected but no internet, 169.254 address (DHCP and DNS)
## Symptom
The device connects to the network but shows "No internet" or "Limited", and
`ipconfig` shows an address starting with 169.254.

## Cause
A 169.254.x.x address is self-assigned when the device gets no reply from DHCP. One
device failing points to its cable, port or driver; many devices on the same network
point to the DHCP server or an exhausted address pool.

## Resolution steps
1. Disconnect and reconnect to trigger a new DHCP request.
2. Run `ipconfig /release` and then `ipconfig /renew`.
3. On a wired desk, try another cable and port.
4. If several devices on the same floor or network get 169.254 addresses, escalate to
   network engineering: the DHCP scope may be full or the server unreachable.

## Warnings
Do not give the device a static IP address as a fix; it can clash with addresses DHCP
hands out later.

claims.claim: `ipconfig /renew` to try and resolve the issue.

cited.title: Laptop cannot see the corporate Wi-Fi network
cited.text:
Laptop cannot see the corporate Wi-Fi network (Wireless access)
## Symptom
Other people in the room are connected, but the corporate network name does not appear
in the user's list of available Wi-Fi networks.

## Cause
The corporate network runs only on the 5 GHz band. An outdated driver, an adapter set to
2.4 GHz only, or airplane mode or a hardware Wi-Fi switch hides it.

## Resolution steps
1. Check that airplane mode is off and the Wi-Fi toggle (or keyboard key) is on.
2. Ask whether other 5 GHz networks are visible. If only 2.4 GHz networks show, check the
   adapter's band setting and set it to auto or 5 GHz preferred.
3. Update the wireless driver from the software centre and restart.
4. If it is still missing, the adapter may be faulty: raise a hardware ticket.

## Warnings
Do not share a phone hotspot with corporate devices as a long-term workaround.

cited.title: Posting period closed for goods movements
cited.text:
Posting period closed for goods movements (Materials and number ranges)
## Symptom
A goods movement fails with a message that posting is only possible in two named
periods, for example the current and the previous month.

## Cause
The materials-management posting period only allows postings in the current and the
previous period. The period is moved forward each month with MMPV. If the month-end
change was not run, or the user picks a date in an older period, the posting is refused.

## Resolution steps
1. Check the posting date the user entered. Ask them to use a date in one of the two
   periods named in the message, if that matches when the movement really happened.
2. If the current calendar month is not among the allowed periods, the period was not
   moved forward. Check the current period with MMRV.
3. Escalate a missing period change to the materials-management team, who run MMPV.
4. Postings into an older closed period need Finance approval and are handled by
   Finance, not the helpdesk.

claims.claim: Ensure it is within the current or previous month.

cited.title: VPN connected but internal sites do not open
cited.text:
VPN connected but internal sites do not open (VPN connectivity)
## Symptom
The VPN client says it is connected, but internal websites, file shares and SAP do not
open. Public websites still work.

## Cause
The VPN tunnel is up but the laptop is not using the internal DNS servers pushed by the
VPN, or a home router uses the same private address range as an internal network, so
traffic for that range never enters the tunnel.

## Resolution steps
1. Ask the user to try an internal resource by IP address. If the IP works but the name
   does not, it is a DNS problem.
2. Run `ipconfig /all` and check that the VPN adapter lists the internal DNS servers.
3. Disconnect and reconnect the VPN; if DNS is still wrong, reinstall the VPN profile from
   the software centre.
4. If even IP addresses fail, compare the home network's address range with the internal
   ranges (for example both using 192.168.1.x). Ask the user to restart the home router
   or test from a hotspot, and report the overlap to network engineering.

claims.claim: Run `ipconfig /all` and check if the internal DNS servers are listed for the VPN adapter.

cited.title: Laptop cannot see the corporate Wi-Fi network
cited.text:
Laptop cannot see the corporate Wi-Fi network (Wireless access)
## Symptom
Other people in the room are connected, but the corporate network name does not appear
in the user's list of available Wi-Fi networks.

## Cause
The corporate network runs only on the 5 GHz band. An outdated driver, an adapter set to
2.4 GHz only, or airplane mode or a hardware Wi-Fi switch hides it.

## Resolution steps
1. Check that airplane mode is off and the Wi-Fi toggle (or keyboard key) is on.
2. Ask whether other 5 GHz networks are visible. If only 2.4 GHz networks show, check the
   adapter's band setting and set it to auto or 5 GHz preferred.
3. Update the wireless driver from the software centre and restart.
4. If it is still missing, the adapter may be faulty: raise a hardware ticket.

## Warnings
Do not share a phone hotspot with corporate devices as a long-term workaround.

cited.title: Office Wi-Fi keeps dropping
cited.text:
Office Wi-Fi keeps dropping (Wireless access)
## Symptom
A laptop repeatedly disconnects from the office Wi-Fi, especially after being idle or
when the user moves between meeting rooms.

## Cause
Most often the adapter's power saving turns the radio down when idle, or the laptop holds
on to a distant access point. When many users in one area drop at once, an access point
or the wireless controller is at fault.

## Resolution steps
1. Ask whether colleagues in the same area are affected. If yes, record the location and
   escalate it as an access point problem.
2. Note the network name and the access point the laptop was last connected to, from the
   connection details.
3. Forget the network and reconnect to clear a stale saved profile.
4. Set the adapter's power management so Windows cannot turn it off to save power, and
   update the wireless driver from the software centre.

## Warnings
Do not tell users to connect to the guest network instead; it has no access to internal
systems.

cited.title: Internet slow for a whole floor
cited.text:
Internet slow for a whole floor (Call quality and file shares)
## Symptom
Many users on the same floor or office report that websites and cloud apps are slow at
the same time.

## Cause
A shared link or switch is saturated: a large download or backup, a faulty uplink running
at reduced speed, or the office internet link reaching capacity.

## Resolution steps
1. Confirm that several users in the same area are affected, and record when it started.
2. Ask whether anything unusual is running: large software deployments, backups or
   video events.
3. Escalate to network engineering with the location, the time and the number of users;
   they check link utilisation and uplink errors.
4. Keep the ticket open as a parent for the other users' reports.

## Warnings
Do not restart network equipment yourself.

cited.title: A query has become slow
cited.text:
A query has become slow (Query performance and indexes)
## Symptom
A report or application feature that used to be fast is now slow, gradually or suddenly
after a release or data growth.

## Cause
The query plan changed: a sequential scan over a large table instead of an index scan,
because an index is missing or table statistics are out of date. Sometimes the query does
far more work than needed.

## Resolution steps
1. Get the exact query from the application log or `pg_stat_statements`.
2. Run `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` on it (on a replica or test copy if it changes data).
3. Look for a sequential scan on a large table where an index scan is expected.
4. If the index exists but is not used, refresh statistics with `ANALYZE` on the table.
5. If an index is missing or the query is inefficient, send the plan to the owning team.

## Warnings
Do not create indexes on production tables without the DBA team; building them can lock
the table.

cited.title: Database server CPU is very high
cited.text:
Database server CPU is very high (Query performance and indexes)
## Symptom
Monitoring shows the database server's CPU near 100 percent and applications are slow.

## Cause
A few expensive queries usually cause most of the load: a new query without a suitable
index, a report run at peak time, or a query whose plan changed after data growth.

## Resolution steps
1. Look at `pg_stat_activity` for long-running active queries right now.
2. Check `pg_stat_statements` for the queries with the highest total execution time.
3. If one report or job causes the spike, ask its owner to stop it or run it off-peak.
4. Send the top queries and their plans to the owning teams for tuning.

## Warnings
Do not restart the database to clear CPU load; it drops every connection and the load
usually returns.

claims.claim: If it's a slow query, run `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` on the query to understand its execution plan.

5. If an index is missing or the query is inefficient, send the plan to the owning team.

## Warnings
Do not create indexes on production tables without the DBA team; building them can lock
the table.

cited.title: Database server CPU is very high
cited.text:
Database server CPU is very high (Query performance and indexes)
## Symptom
Monitoring shows the database server's CPU near 100 percent and applications are slow.

## Cause
A few expensive queries usually cause most of the load: a new query without a suitable
index, a report run at peak time, or a query whose plan changed after data growth.

## Resolution steps
1. Look at `pg_stat_activity` for long-running active queries right now.
2. Check `pg_stat_statements` for the queries with the highest total execution time.
3. If one report or job causes the spike, ask its owner to stop it or run it off-peak.
4. Send the top queries and their plans to the owning teams for tuning.

## Warnings
Do not restart the database to clear CPU load; it drops every connection and the load
usually returns.

cited.title: Health insurance claim status
cited.text:
Health insurance claim status (Benefits and insurance)
## Symptom
An employee asks how to file a health insurance claim, or why one is still not paid.

## Cause
Claims are processed by the insurance carrier, not by HR. In-network providers file
claims themselves; other claims are submitted by the employee in the carrier's portal.

## Resolution steps
1. Ask whether the provider was in-network. If yes, the provider files the claim.
2. For other claims, the employee submits through the carrier's portal with an itemised
   bill and proof of payment.
3. For status, the employee checks the carrier's portal using the claim number.
4. If a claim is beyond the carrier's stated turnaround time, HR escalates it through the
   carrier's employer support line, quoting the claim number only.

## Warnings
Never ask for or record medical details in a ticket; use the claim number only.

cited.title: How performance reviews work
cited.text:
How performance reviews work (Workplace policy and reviews)
## Symptom
An employee or manager asks when reviews happen, how ratings are decided, or when pay
changes are announced.

## Cause
Reviews follow an annual cycle with a mid-year check-in. Ratings are calibrated across
teams before they are shared. Pay decisions are communicated separately.

## Resolution steps
1. Explain the steps: self-assessment, manager assessment, calibration, then the rating is
   shared.
2. New hires in their first 90 days get a probation check-in instead of a formal review.
3. Pay changes are announced in a separate communication after the cycle, on their own
   timeline.
4. Disagreements with a rating are raised with the manager first, then with HR.

## Warnings
Do not predict pay changes from a rating.

cited.title: Writes fail because a storage quota is reached
cited.text:
Writes fail because a storage quota is reached (Object storage)
## Symptom
An application or backup job fails with a quota or limit error, or writes start failing
while reads still work.

## Cause
A limit was reached: an account-level service quota, a size limit on a volume or file
share, or a budget control that stops further spending.

## Resolution steps
1. Read the error to identify which limit was hit.
2. Check whether old data can be archived or deleted under the retention policy before
   asking for more space.
3. Request a service quota increase through the cloud provider's process. It is not
   instant, so state clearly if production is blocked.
4. If usage grows steadily, raise a capacity-planning review instead of repeated small
   increases.

## Warnings
Do not request the largest possible quota "to be safe"; it hides runaway growth.

claims.claim: Review the application's retention policy and consider archiving or deleting old data.

Posting period error on goods movement

Failed to post goods movement; system says only current and previous periods are allowed. Check if month-end process ran correctly to resolve.

claims.claim: Check the posting date the user entered.

cited.title: Posting period closed for goods movements
cited.text:
Posting period closed for goods movements (Materials and number ranges)
## Symptom
A goods movement fails with a message that posting is only possible in two named
periods, for example the current and the previous month.

## Cause
The materials-management posting period only allows postings in the current and the
previous period. The period is moved forward each month with MMPV. If the month-end
change was not run, or the user picks a date in an older period, the posting is refused.

## Resolution steps
1. Check the posting date the user entered. Ask them to use a date in one of the two
   periods named in the message, if that matches when the movement really happened.
2. If the current calendar month is not among the allowed periods, the period was not
   moved forward. Check the current period with MMRV.
3. Escalate a missing period change to the materials-management team, who run MMPV.
4. Postings into an older closed period need Finance approval and are handled by
   Finance, not the helpdesk.

claims.claim: Ensure it is within the current or previous period.

IDoc status 51

Inbound IDoc in WE02 shows status 51. Order not posted; check WE05. What master data is missing? What master data is missing for this IDoc, specifically a customer or vendor detail issue?

claims.claim: Open the IDoc in WE02 and read the status record for status 51.

cited.title: IDoc in status 51
cited.text:
IDoc in status 51 (Batch jobs and IDocs)
## Symptom
An inbound IDoc shows status 51, "Application document not posted", in WE02 or WE05,
and the expected order, delivery or invoice was never created.

## Cause
The IDoc arrived but the application could not post it. Typical reasons are missing
master data (customer, vendor or material), a missing pricing condition, or a partner
profile mismatch.

## Resolution steps
1. Open the IDoc in WE02 and read the status record for status 51. The error message
   usually names the missing field or master record.
2. Fix the cause, or ask the master-data team to create the missing record.
3. Reprocess the IDoc with BD87.
4. If many IDocs from the same partner fail at once, check the partner profile and any
   recent mapping change instead of fixing IDocs one by one.

## Warnings
Do not reprocess an IDoc repeatedly without reading the error. If the cause was
intermittent, repeated attempts can create duplicate documents.

claims.claim: Check if the error message names a missing customer, vendor, or material detail.

Internal Sites Not Opening

Connected to the VPN but can't access internal sites or file shares. Public internet works fine, but internal SAP is unreachable. The internal sites should be on the tunnel but aren't. Laptop’s DNS settings might be the issue, but I can’t figure out how to fix it. Checked the routing tables, but they look correct to me. The internal network uses the same address range as my home router. Why isn't the traffic going through the tunnel for the internal sites? Why isn't the traffic going through the tunnel for the internal sites?

claims.claim: Try accessing the internal resource by IP address.

cited.title: VPN connected but internal sites do not open
cited.text:
VPN connected but internal sites do not open (VPN connectivity)
## Symptom
The VPN client says it is connected, but internal websites, file shares and SAP do not
open. Public websites still work.

## Cause
The VPN tunnel is up but the laptop is not using the internal DNS servers pushed by the
VPN, or a home router uses the same private address range as an internal network, so
traffic for that range never enters the tunnel.

## Resolution steps
1. Ask the user to try an internal resource by IP address. If the IP works but the name
   does not, it is a DNS problem.
2. Run `ipconfig /all` and check that the VPN adapter lists the internal DNS servers.
3. Disconnect and reconnect the VPN; if DNS is still wrong, reinstall the VPN profile from
   the software centre.
4. If even IP addresses fail, compare the home network's address range with the internal
   ranges (for example both using 192.168.1.x). Ask the user to restart the home router
   or test from a hotspot, and report the overlap to network engineering.

cited.text:
VPN connected but internal sites do not open (VPN connectivity)
## Symptom
The VPN client says it is connected, but internal websites, file shares and SAP do not
open. Public websites still work.

## Cause
The VPN tunnel is up but the laptop is not using the internal DNS servers pushed by the
VPN, or a home router uses the same private address range as an internal network, so
traffic for that range never enters the tunnel.

## Resolution steps
1. Ask the user to try an internal resource by IP address. If the IP works but the name
   does not, it is a DNS problem.
2. Run `ipconfig /all` and check that the VPN adapter lists the internal DNS servers.
3. Disconnect and reconnect the VPN; if DNS is still wrong, reinstall the VPN profile from
   the software centre.
4. If even IP addresses fail, compare the home network's address range with the internal
   ranges (for example both using 192.168.1.x). Ask the user to restart the home router
   or test from a hotspot, and report the overlap to network engineering.

cited.title: Not authorised for a transaction
cited.text:
Not authorised for a transaction (User access and authorisations)
## Symptom
Starting a transaction fails with "You are not authorized to use transaction XXXX", or
an action inside a transaction fails with a missing-authorization message.

## Cause
The user's roles do not contain the authorization object and values that the
transaction checks. This often happens after a job change, or when a new transaction is
rolled out without a matching role.

## Resolution steps
1. Ask the user to reproduce the error and then immediately run transaction SU53. It
   shows the last failed authorization check: the object, field and value that were missing.
2. Ask for a screenshot of SU53 and the transaction code.
3. Confirm with the user's manager that the access fits the user's job. New access always
   needs manager approval, recorded in the access-request ticket.
4. Raise a role-change request to the SAP security team with the SU53 screenshot, the
   transaction code and the business justification.
5. When the role is assigned, ask the user to log off and log on again so the new
   authorizations are loaded.

Developer tool failing

Developer tool fails with SSL error at work. Works at home; only issues here. Error: 'unable to get local issuer certificate'. Other tools work fine on network. Some apps need specific certificates. Why won't this tool trust our cert? What specific setting do I need to adjust for this tool to work?

claims.claim: Confirm the error appears only on the office network or VPN.

cited.title: Certificate errors in a desktop tool on the office network
cited.text:
Certificate errors in a desktop tool on the office network (Firewall and proxy)
## Symptom
A developer tool, command-line client or desktop app fails with an SSL or certificate
error ("unable to get local issuer certificate", "self-signed certificate in chain") on
the office network, but works at home.

## Cause
The web proxy inspects encrypted traffic and re-signs it with the company's root
certificate. Browsers trust that certificate, but some tools use their own certificate
store and do not.

## Resolution steps
1. Confirm the error appears only on the office network or VPN.
2. Point the tool at the company root certificate, which is published on the intranet
   (most tools have a setting or environment variable for a CA bundle).
3. If the tool cannot be configured, raise a request for an inspection bypass for that
   domain, with the business reason.

## Warnings
Never turn off certificate verification in the tool; it removes protection against
real interception.

cited.title: Database disk almost full
cited.text:
Database disk almost full (Disk space and backups)
## Symptom
Monitoring warns the database volume is nearly full, or the database already rejects
writes because the disk is full.

## Cause
Table and index bloat, write-ahead log (WAL) files piling up because a replication slot
or WAL archiving is stuck, or genuine data growth.

## Resolution steps
1. Find what uses the space: data files, or the `pg_wal` directory.
2. If `pg_wal` is large, check `pg_replication_slots` for inactive slots and WAL archiving
   for failures.
3. If writes are already failing, expand the volume first to restore service.
4. Then fix the cause: remove an abandoned slot (after the DBA confirms), fix archiving,
   or address bloat.

## Warnings
Never delete files from `pg_wal` by hand; it can make the database impossible to start.

claims.claim: If an inactive slot is found, contact the DBA to confirm if it can be safely removed.

cited.title: WAL archiving failing
cited.text:
WAL archiving failing (Disk space and backups)
## Symptom
Monitoring reports WAL archive failures, and the `pg_wal` directory keeps growing.

## Cause
PostgreSQL keeps each WAL file until `archive_command` succeeds for it. If the archive
target is full, unreachable or its credentials expired, WAL files pile up locally.

## Resolution steps
1. Check `pg_stat_archiver` for `failed_count` and `last_failed_wal`.
2. Read the database log for the archive command's error message.
3. Fix the target: free space, restore network access, or renew the credential.
4. Confirm that archiving resumes and `pg_wal` shrinks as old files are archived.

## Warnings
Point-in-time recovery is broken while archiving fails; treat it as urgent.

cited.title: Application runs out of database connections
cited.text:
Application runs out of database connections (Connections and pools)
## Symptom
Application logs show "connection pool exhausted", "sorry, too many clients already", or
requests waiting for a database connection, while the database server is up.

## Cause
Either the database reached `max_connections`, or the application's pool is full because
code paths take connections and never return them (a leak), often after an unhandled
error. Sessions left "idle in transaction" also hold connection slots.

## Resolution steps
1. Compare the number of connections in `pg_stat_activity` with `SHOW max_connections`.
2. Group the sessions by application and state; many "idle in transaction" sessions from
   one application point to that application.
3. Check whether the errors started after a deployment; a new code path that does not
   close its connection is the usual cause.
4. As a stop-gap, restart the affected application instance to release leaked connections.
5. Send the findings to the owning team to fix the leak or pool settings.

## Warnings
Raising `max_connections` hides a leak and costs memory on the server; fix the leak first.

cited.text:
Laptop cannot see the corporate Wi-Fi network (Wireless access)
## Symptom
Other people in the room are connected, but the corporate network name does not appear
in the user's list of available Wi-Fi networks.

## Cause
The corporate network runs only on the 5 GHz band. An outdated driver, an adapter set to
2.4 GHz only, or airplane mode or a hardware Wi-Fi switch hides it.

## Resolution steps
1. Check that airplane mode is off and the Wi-Fi toggle (or keyboard key) is on.
2. Ask whether other 5 GHz networks are visible. If only 2.4 GHz networks show, check the
   adapter's band setting and set it to auto or 5 GHz preferred.
3. Update the wireless driver from the software centre and restart.
4. If it is still missing, the adapter may be faulty: raise a hardware ticket.

## Warnings
Do not share a phone hotspot with corporate devices as a long-term workaround.

cited.title: Connected but no internet, 169.254 address
cited.text:
Connected but no internet, 169.254 address (DHCP and DNS)
## Symptom
The device connects to the network but shows "No internet" or "Limited", and
`ipconfig` shows an address starting with 169.254.

## Cause
A 169.254.x.x address is self-assigned when the device gets no reply from DHCP. One
device failing points to its cable, port or driver; many devices on the same network
point to the DHCP server or an exhausted address pool.

## Resolution steps
1. Disconnect and reconnect to trigger a new DHCP request.
2. Run `ipconfig /release` and then `ipconfig /renew`.
3. On a wired desk, try another cable and port.
4. If several devices on the same floor or network get 169.254 addresses, escalate to
   network engineering: the DHCP scope may be full or the server unreachable.

## Warnings
Do not give the device a static IP address as a fix; it can clash with addresses DHCP
hands out later.

cited.title: Video calls freeze or lag
cited.text:
Video calls freeze or lag (Call quality and file shares)
## Symptom
Video and audio calls freeze, drop or lag, while web browsing seems normal.

## Cause
Calls need low latency more than bandwidth. Weak Wi-Fi, large uploads on the same
connection, or VPN routing for a call that does not need it are the usual causes. If a
whole office is affected, the internet link is saturated.

## Resolution steps
1. Ask whether it happens on a cable too. If only on Wi-Fi, treat it as a Wi-Fi signal
   problem (move closer to an access point, or use a cable).
2. Check for large uploads or backups running at the same time.
3. If the user is on VPN for a call with outside participants, they can disconnect the VPN
   for the call.
4. Ask the user to run the call app's network test during a bad call and send the result.
5. If many users at one office are affected, escalate as a link-capacity problem.

## Warnings
Do not ask users to stop company backups to free bandwidth.

cited.title: Office Wi-Fi keeps dropping
cited.text:
Office Wi-Fi keeps dropping (Wireless access)
## Symptom
A laptop repeatedly disconnects from the office Wi-Fi, especially after being idle or
when the user moves between meeting rooms.

## Cause
Most often the adapter's power saving turns the radio down when idle, or the laptop holds
on to a distant access point. When many users in one area drop at once, an access point
or the wireless controller is at fault.

## Resolution steps
1. Ask whether colleagues in the same area are affected. If yes, record the location and
   escalate it as an access point problem.
2. Note the network name and the access point the laptop was last connected to, from the
   connection details.
3. Forget the network and reconnect to clear a stale saved profile.
4. Set the adapter's power management so Windows cannot turn it off to save power, and
   update the wireless driver from the software centre.

## Warnings
Do not tell users to connect to the guest network instead; it has no access to internal
systems.

Laptop cannot see the corporate Wi-Fi network (Wireless access)
## Symptom
Other people in the room are connected, but the corporate network name does not appear
in the user's list of available Wi-Fi networks.

## Cause
The corporate network runs only on the 5 GHz band. An outdated driver, an adapter set to
2.4 GHz only, or airplane mode or a hardware Wi-Fi switch hides it.

## Resolution steps
1. Check that airplane mode is off and the Wi-Fi toggle (or keyboard key) is on.
2. Ask whether other 5 GHz networks are visible. If only 2.4 GHz networks show, check the
   adapter's band setting and set it to auto or 5 GHz preferred.
3. Update the wireless driver from the software centre and restart.
4. If it is still missing, the adapter may be faulty: raise a hardware ticket.

## Warnings
Do not share a phone hotspot with corporate devices as a long-term workaround.

claims.claim: Update the wireless driver from the software centre and restart.

drafts.ticket:
Intranet not working

Cannot access internal servers by name, only IP. Public sites work fine; just internal names are failing. Also getting lots of pop-up ads lately, very distracting.

claims.claim: Check if your device is connected to the corporate network or the VPN.

cited.title: Internal names do not resolve
cited.text:
Internal names do not resolve (DHCP and DNS)
## Symptom
Public websites work, but internal names such as the intranet or a file server do not
open. The same resource opens when the user types its IP address.

## Cause
The device is not using the internal DNS servers: it is off the corporate network or VPN,
or it has public DNS servers set, which cannot resolve internal names.

## Resolution steps
1. Confirm the device is on the corporate network or connected to the VPN.
2. Run `ipconfig /all` and check that the DNS servers are the internal ones, not public
   resolvers such as 8.8.8.8.
3. If public DNS servers were set by hand, set the adapter back to obtain DNS
   automatically.
4. Run `ipconfig /flushdns` and retry.

## Warnings
Once the IP address works but the name does not, do not keep checking cables and Wi-Fi;
it is a DNS problem.

cited.title: VPN connected but internal sites do not open
cited.text:
VPN connected but internal sites do not open (VPN connectivity)
## Symptom
The VPN client says it is connected, but internal websites, file shares and SAP do not
open. Public websites still work.

## Cause
The VPN tunnel is up but the laptop is not using the internal DNS servers pushed by the
VPN, or a home router uses the same private address range as an internal network, so
traffic for that range never enters the tunnel.

## Resolution steps
1. Ask the user to try an internal resource by IP address. If the IP works but the name
   does not, it is a DNS problem.
2. Run `ipconfig /all` and check that the VPN adapter lists the internal DNS servers.
3. Disconnect and reconnect the VPN; if DNS is still wrong, reinstall the VPN profile from
   the software centre.
4. If even IP addresses fail, compare the home network's address range with the internal
   ranges (for example both using 192.168.1.x). Ask the user to restart the home router
   or test from a hotspot, and report the overlap to network engineering.

claims.claim: Run `ipconfig /all` to verify the DNS servers are set to the internal ones.

SSL errors in desktop tool

Developer tool faiils with SSL errors on office network. Works fine at home. Error: 'unable to get local issuer certificate'. Network proxy issues? Confirmed at home connection. Logs: 2026-03-15 14:45:02 [ERR] unable to get local issuer certificate

claims.claim: Check if the company root certificate is published on the intranet.

cited.title: Certificate errors in a desktop tool on the office network
cited.text:
Certificate errors in a desktop tool on the office network (Firewall and proxy)
## Symptom
A developer tool, command-line client or desktop app fails with an SSL or certificate
error ("unable to get local issuer certificate", "self-signed certificate in chain") on
the office network, but works at home.

## Cause
The web proxy inspects encrypted traffic and re-signs it with the company's root
certificate. Browsers trust that certificate, but some tools use their own certificate
store and do not.

## Resolution steps
1. Confirm the error appears only on the office network or VPN.
2. Point the tool at the company root certificate, which is published on the intranet
   (most tools have a setting or environment variable for a CA bundle).
3. If the tool cannot be configured, raise a request for an inspection bypass for that
   domain, with the business reason.

## Warnings
Never turn off certificate verification in the tool; it removes protection against
real interception.

Index errors on sales_data

Queries return wrong results. Logs show index errors. Issue occurs after crashes or power loss. Sales reports inconsistent. Affects daily sales analysis. Need fix asap.

claims.claim: Run the query again with index scans disabled: `SET enable_indexscan = off

cited.title: Index returns wrong results
cited.text:
Index returns wrong results (Query performance and indexes)
## Symptom
Queries return inconsistent or clearly wrong results, or the log shows index errors.

## Cause
The index is corrupted, usually after a crash, power loss or a storage fault during a write.

## Resolution steps
1. Run the query again with index scans disabled for the session
   (`SET enable_indexscan = off; SET enable_bitmapscan = off;`). If the results differ, the
   index is at fault.
2. Rebuild it with `REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY` so the table stays usable.
3. Find out why it happened: check the logs for crashes or storage errors.
4. If corruption comes back on the same storage, escalate to the storage team.

## Warnings
A plain `REINDEX` locks the table; use the concurrent form, or schedule a quiet window.

claims.claim: SET enable_bitmapscan = off;`.

drafts.ticket:
Payslip not found

I can't find my payslip for this month. I checked my account but it's not there. Is it supposed to be published today? I joined last month, did it get sent separately? When will my pay be credited? Will I get the payslip after payment? Can someone help me?

claims.claim: Check the HR portal under Payroll Payslips.

cited.title: Payslip missing or pay date question
cited.text:
Payslip missing or pay date question (Payroll and timesheets)
## Symptom
An employee cannot find this month's payslip, or asks when salary will be paid.

## Cause
Salary is paid on the last working day of the month and payslips are published two
working days before that. A missing payslip usually means it is not published yet, or the
employee joined or left mid-month and was paid in a separate run.

## Resolution steps
1. Check today's date against the pay date; payslips appear two working days before it.
2. Direct the employee to the HR portal under Payroll, then Payslips.
3. If the pay date has passed and the payslip is missing, check whether the employee was
   in a special run (mid-month starter or leaver) before escalating to payroll.
4. Questions about the amount go to payroll with the specific line item.

## Warnings
Never share payslip or salary details with anyone except the employee.

claims.claim: If the payslip is still not there, confirm if you joined or left mid-month.

drafts.ticket:
Goods receipt failing

When trying to receive goods in MIGO, the system says the PO item is blocked. I need to post receipts quickly to keep inventory accurate. Other items from the same PO are posting fine. Not sure if I’m missing a step or if this is an issue with the purchase order. Have ben looking at the ME22N screen but can’t find the item in question. Is there a way to unblock items from the goods receipt screen? What’s the usual process for resolving this issue? What’s the usual process for resolving this issue?

claims.claim: Display the purchase order in ME23N and open the item to check for any block or deletion indicator.

cited.title: Goods receipt fails because the PO item is blocked
cited.text:
Goods receipt fails because the PO item is blocked (Purchasing and goods receipt)
## Symptom
Posting a goods receipt in MIGO against a purchase order fails with a message that the
purchase order item is blocked, so the goods cannot be received.

## Cause
A buyer has blocked the PO item in ME22N (for example during a dispute with the
vendor), or the item has a deletion indicator. Blocked items cannot be received until a
buyer releases them.

## Resolution steps
1. Display the PO in ME23N and open the item. Check whether the item shows a block or a
   deletion indicator in the item overview.
2. Find the buyer from the PO header (purchasing group) and ask whether the block is
   intentional.
3. If the block should be removed, the buyer removes it in ME22N and saves the PO.
4. Retry the goods receipt in MIGO.
5. If the item has a deletion indicator and the goods have physically arrived, the buyer
   must create a new PO item; a deleted item cannot be received.

claims.claim: If a block is found, contact the buyer to request the block be removed in ME22N.

Incorrect date & number format in SAP

SAP is displaying dates as month/day/year, not day/month/year, causing confusion. Numbers with decimals are also incorrect, using commas instead of periods. This affects our daily reporting and financial downloads significantly. We follow regional settings, but SAP shows these incorrect formats. How long can this discrepancy persist before it needs to be fixed? How long can this discrepancy persist before it needs to be fixed?

claims.claim: Open transaction SU3 (own user data) and go to the Defaults tab.

cited.title: Wrong date or number format in SAP
cited.text:
Wrong date or number format in SAP (GUI, dumps and printing)
## Symptom
SAP shows dates as month/day/year instead of day/month/year, or uses a comma instead of a
decimal point, so amounts look ten or a thousand times wrong in downloads.

## Cause
Date and decimal formats are personal settings stored in the user's master record; they
may differ from Windows regional settings.

## Resolution steps
1. Open transaction SU3 (own user data) and go to the Defaults tab.
2. Choose the correct decimal notation and date format.
3. Save, then log off and log on again so the new settings apply.
4. Re-export any spreadsheet downloads made with the wrong format.

## Warnings
The formats affect only how values are displayed and exported, not the stored data; do
not correct postings because of a display format.

claims.claim: Choose the correct decimal notation and date format.

drafts.ticket:
Error accessing transaction ZXY123

Trying to run transaction ZXY123 results in 'Not authorized' error. Checked roles but can't finnd relevant authorization object. Last role update was two weeks ago; no changes since then. When will the new transaction be fully rolled out? When will the new transaction be fully rolled out?

claims.claim: Run transaction SU53 to identify the missing authorization object.

cited.title: Not authorised for a transaction
cited.text:
Not authorised for a transaction (User access and authorisations)
## Symptom
Starting a transaction fails with "You are not authorized to use transaction XXXX", or
an action inside a transaction fails with a missing-authorization message.

## Cause
The user's roles do not contain the authorization object and values that the
transaction checks. This often happens after a job change, or when a new transaction is
rolled out without a matching role.

## Resolution steps
1. Ask the user to reproduce the error and then immediately run transaction SU53. It
   shows the last failed authorization check: the object, field and value that were missing.
2. Ask for a screenshot of SU53 and the transaction code.
3. Confirm with the user's manager that the access fits the user's job. New access always
   needs manager approval, recorded in the access-request ticket.
4. Raise a role-change request to the SAP security team with the SU53 screenshot, the
   transaction code and the business justification.
5. When the role is assigned, ask the user to log off and log on again so the new
   authorizations are loaded.

claims.claim: Take a screenshot of the SU53 output and the transaction code ZXY123.

drafts.ticket:
SSL errors in dev tool

Developer tool fails with 'self-signed certificate in chain' error on office network. Works fine at home. Network setup causes issues. Can this be fixed by adding an exception in the tool settings, or do I need network changes?

claims.claim: Confirm the error appears only on the office network or VPN.

cited.title: Certificate errors in a desktop tool on the office network
cited.text:
Certificate errors in a desktop tool on the office network (Firewall and proxy)
## Symptom
A developer tool, command-line client or desktop app fails with an SSL or certificate
error ("unable to get local issuer certificate", "self-signed certificate in chain") on
the office network, but works at home.

## Cause
The web proxy inspects encrypted traffic and re-signs it with the company's root
certificate. Browsers trust that certificate, but some tools use their own certificate
store and do not.

## Resolution steps
1. Confirm the error appears only on the office network or VPN.
2. Point the tool at the company root certificate, which is published on the intranet
   (most tools have a setting or environment variable for a CA bundle).
3. If the tool cannot be configured, raise a request for an inspection bypass for that
   domain, with the business reason.

## Warnings
Never turn off certificate verification in the tool; it removes protection against
real interception.

drafts.ticket:
Posting blocked: GL account issue

Cannot post journal entries for Q4 financials. Error message: 'Account blocked for posting'. Checked FS00, the account is marked for retirement. Tried unlocking but got the same error. Need help unblocking the account or a workaround.

claims.claim: Check the GL account in FS00 to confirm it is marked for retirement.

cited.title: Posting period closed for goods movements
cited.text:
Posting period closed for goods movements (Materials and number ranges)
## Symptom
A goods movement fails with a message that posting is only possible in two named
periods, for example the current and the previous month.

## Cause
The materials-management posting period only allows postings in the current and the
previous period. The period is moved forward each month with MMPV. If the month-end
change was not run, or the user picks a date in an older period, the posting is refused.

## Resolution steps
1. Check the posting date the user entered. Ask them to use a date in one of the two
   periods named in the message, if that matches when the movement really happened.
2. If the current calendar month is not among the allowed periods, the period was not
   moved forward. Check the current period with MMRV.
3. Escalate a missing period change to the materials-management team, who run MMPV.
4. Postings into an older closed period need Finance approval and are handled by
   Finance, not the helpdesk.

claims.claim: Contact the buyer responsible for the account to determine if the block is intentional.

cited.title: Goods receipt fails because the PO item is blocked
cited.text:
Goods receipt fails because the PO item is blocked (Purchasing and goods receipt)
## Symptom
Posting a goods receipt in MIGO against a purchase order fails with a message that the
purchase order item is blocked, so the goods cannot be received.

## Cause
A buyer has blocked the PO item in ME22N (for example during a dispute with the
vendor), or the item has a deletion indicator. Blocked items cannot be received until a
buyer releases them.

## Resolution steps
1. Display the PO in ME23N and open the item. Check whether the item shows a block or a
   deletion indicator in the item overview.
2. Find the buyer from the PO header (purchasing group) and ask whether the block is
   intentional.
3. If the block should be removed, the buyer removes it in ME22N and saves the PO.
4. Retry the goods receipt in MIGO.
5. If the item has a deletion indicator and the goods have physically arrived, the buyer
   must create a new PO item; a deleted item cannot be received.

claims.claim: If the block is not intentional, ask the buyer to release the account in ME22N.

drafts.ticket:
Inactive Replication Slot

Monitoring shows our replication slot is inactive. Disk space on the primary is rapidly growing. This means WAL isn't being consumed by a replica or subscriber. Need to fix this ASAP to avoid space issues and delays. Someone must investigate the missing consumer.

claims.claim: Check the `pg_replication_slots` to identify any inactive slots.

cited.title: Database disk almost full
cited.text:
Database disk almost full (Disk space and backups)
## Symptom
Monitoring warns the database volume is nearly full, or the database already rejects
writes because the disk is full.

## Cause
Table and index bloat, write-ahead log (WAL) files piling up because a replication slot
or WAL archiving is stuck, or genuine data growth.

## Resolution steps
1. Find what uses the space: data files, or the `pg_wal` directory.
2. If `pg_wal` is large, check `pg_replication_slots` for inactive slots and WAL archiving
   for failures.
3. If writes are already failing, expand the volume first to restore service.
4. Then fix the cause: remove an abandoned slot (after the DBA confirms), fix archiving,
   or address bloat.

## Warnings
Never delete files from `pg_wal` by hand; it can make the database impossible to start.

cited.title: WAL archiving failing
cited.text:
WAL archiving failing (Disk space and backups)
## Symptom
Monitoring reports WAL archive failures, and the `pg_wal` directory keeps growing.

## Cause
PostgreSQL keeps each WAL file until `archive_command` succeeds for it. If the archive
target is full, unreachable or its credentials expired, WAL files pile up locally.

## Resolution steps
1. Check `pg_stat_archiver` for `failed_count` and `last_failed_wal`.
2. Read the database log for the archive command's error message.
3. Fix the target: free space, restore network access, or renew the credential.
4. Confirm that archiving resumes and `pg_wal` shrinks as old files are archived.

## Warnings
Point-in-time recovery is broken while archiving fails; treat it as urgent.

claims.claim: Verify if WAL archiving is failing by checking `pg_stat_archiver`.

drafts.ticket:
Database connections full

Our app keeps timing out when trying to connect to the managed DB. Need help figring out why so many connections are stuck.

claims.claim: Check the number of active connections in `pg_stat_activity` and compare it with `SHOW max_connections`.

cited.title: Application runs out of database connections
cited.text:
Application runs out of database connections (Connections and pools)
## Symptom
Application logs show "connection pool exhausted", "sorry, too many clients already", or
requests waiting for a database connection, while the database server is up.

## Cause
Either the database reached `max_connections`, or the application's pool is full because
code paths take connections and never return them (a leak), often after an unhandled
error. Sessions left "idle in transaction" also hold connection slots.

## Resolution steps
1. Compare the number of connections in `pg_stat_activity` with `SHOW max_connections`.
2. Group the sessions by application and state; many "idle in transaction" sessions from
   one application point to that application.
3. Check whether the errors started after a deployment; a new code path that does not
   close its connection is the usual cause.
4. As a stop-gap, restart the affected application instance to release leaked connections.
5. Send the findings to the owning team to fix the leak or pool settings.

## Warnings
Raising `max_connections` hides a leak and costs memory on the server; fix the leak first.

claims.claim: Group the sessions by application and state to identify any 'idle in transaction' sessions.

cited.title: Application runs out of database connections
cited.text:
Application runs out of database connections (Connections and pools)
## Symptom
Application logs show "connection pool exhausted", "sorry, too many clients already", or
requests waiting for a database connection, while the database server is up.

## Cause
Either the database reached `max_connections`, or the application's pool is full because
code paths take connections and never return them (a leak), often after an unhandled
error. Sessions left "idle in transaction" also hold connection slots.

## Resolution steps
1. Compare the number of connections in `pg_stat_activity` with `SHOW max_connections`.
2. Group the sessions by application and state; many "idle in transaction" sessions from
   one application point to that application.
3. Check whether the errors started after a deployment; a new code path that does not
   close its connection is the usual cause.
4. As a stop-gap, restart the affected application instance to release leaked connections.
5. Send the findings to the owning team to fix the leak or pool settings.

## Warnings
Raising `max_connections` hides a leak and costs memory on the server; fix the leak first.

cited.title: Internet slow for a whole floor
cited.text:
Internet slow for a whole floor (Call quality and file shares)
## Symptom
Many users on the same floor or office report that websites and cloud apps are slow at
the same time.

## Cause
A shared link or switch is saturated: a large download or backup, a faulty uplink running
at reduced speed, or the office internet link reaching capacity.

1. Confirm that several users in the same area are affected, and record when it started.
2. Ask whether anything unusual is running: large software deployments, backups or
   video events.

cited.title: Office Wi-Fi keeps dropping
cited.text:
Office Wi-Fi keeps dropping (Wireless access)
## Symptom
A laptop repeatedly disconnects from the office Wi-Fi, especially after being idle or
when the user moves between meeting rooms.

## Cause
Most often the adapter's power saving turns the radio down when idle, or the laptop holds
on to a distant access point. When many users in one area drop at once, an access point
or the wireless controller is at fault.

## Resolution steps
1. Ask whether colleagues in the same area are affected. If yes, record the location and
   escalate it as an access point problem.
2. Note the network name and the access point the laptop was last connected to, from the
   connection details.
3. Forget the network and reconnect to clear a stale saved profile.
4. Set the adapter's power management so Windows cannot turn it off to save power, and
   update the wireless driver from the software centre.

## Warnings
Do not tell users to connect to the guest network instead; it has no access to internal
systems.

claims.claim: Run a network test during a video call to identify any issues.

cited.title: Video calls freeze or lag
cited.text:
Video calls freeze or lag (Call quality and file shares)
## Symptom
Video and audio calls freeze, drop or lag, while web browsing seems normal.

## Cause
Calls need low latency more than bandwidth. Weak Wi-Fi, large uploads on the same
connection, or VPN routing for a call that does not need it are the usual causes. If a
whole office is affected, the internet link is saturated.

## Resolution steps
1. Ask whether it happens on a cable too. If only on Wi-Fi, treat it as a Wi-Fi signal
   problem (move closer to an access point, or use a cable).
2. Check for large uploads or backups running at the same time.
3. If the user is on VPN for a call with outside participants, they can disconnect the VPN
   for the call.
4. Ask the user to run the call app's network test during a bad call and send the result.
5. If many users at one office are affected, escalate as a link-capacity problem.

## Warnings
Do not ask users to stop company backups to free bandwidth.

The new approval process is causing delays in our project. Also, our printer keeps going offline for no reason.

claims.claim: Check the approval status of the purchase order in ME23N.

cited.title: Purchase order waiting for release
cited.text:
Purchase order waiting for release (Purchasing and goods receipt)
## Symptom
A new purchase order cannot be printed or sent to the vendor, and goods cannot be
received against it. ME23N shows a release strategy on the PO header.

## Cause
POs above a value limit go through a release strategy. Until every required approver has
released it, the PO stays blocked for output and follow-on documents.

## Resolution steps
1. Open the PO in ME23N and go to the Release Strategy tab in the header. It lists each
   release code and shows which are still outstanding.
2. Tell the requester who the outstanding approver is and ask them to follow up.
3. Approvers release individual POs in ME29N or several at once in ME28. Editing the PO
   is not a release.
4. If the approver is away, the deputy configured for that release code can release on
   their behalf.

## Warnings
The helpdesk cannot release a PO for an approver. Changing the PO value to get under the
release limit is a policy violation.

claims.claim: If the printer is offline, contact desktop support for assistance.

cited.title: Printed SAP document never arrives at the printer
cited.text:
Printed SAP document never arrives at the printer (GUI, dumps and printing)
## Symptom
A user printed an invoice, purchase order or delivery note from SAP but nothing came out
of the printer.

## Cause
SAP creates a spool request and passes it to the output device. The request can fail
(wrong output device), wait for a printer that is offline, or never be created because
no output was triggered for the document.

## Resolution steps
1. Open SP01 and search for spool requests by the user's ID and the time of printing.
2. If a request exists with an error status, open its log. The most common cause is an
   output device that points to the wrong or a retired printer.
3. If the request is fine, reprint it from SP01 to the correct output device.
4. If no spool request exists, the print was never triggered from SAP. Check the
   document's output messages; an output type may be missing.
5. If the printer is offline or out of paper, hand over to desktop support.

claims.claim: If the SAP document was not triggered, check the document's output messages for missing output types.

claims.claim: Check the application logs on the servers for any crashes or restarts.

cited.title: Website returns 502 or 503 from the load balancer
cited.text:
Website returns 502 or 503 from the load balancer (Load balancers and certificates)
## Symptom
Users get "502 Bad Gateway", "503 Service Unavailable" or "504 Gateway Timeout" from an
application behind a cloud load balancer.

## Cause
The code shows where it failed. 503 means the load balancer has no healthy servers. 502
means a server closed the connection or sent an invalid response. 504 means the server
did not answer within the load balancer's timeout.

## Resolution steps
1. Note the exact error code and when it started.
2. For 503, check the target group: if no servers are healthy, follow the unhealthy-server
   article.
3. For 502, check the application logs on the servers for crashes or restarts at that time.
4. For 504, check for slow requests or a dependency (database, external API) that slowed
   down.
5. Send the findings to the application's owning team.

## Warnings
Do not raise the load balancer timeout to hide 504 errors without the owning team.

claims.claim: Verify the health check path, port, and expected status code in the target settings.

cited.title: Load balancer marks servers unhealthy
cited.text:
Load balancer marks servers unhealthy (Load balancers and certificates)
## Symptom
The load balancer marks one or more backend servers unhealthy, so capacity drops or
requests fail intermittently.

## Cause
The health check request fails: the application does not answer the configured path with
the expected status code, it answers too slowly, or a security group blocks the load
balancer from reaching the server.

## Resolution steps
1. Check the health check path, port and expected status code in the target settings.
2. Call that path directly on an affected server and check the response code and time.
3. If the server answers correctly but is still unhealthy, check the security group allows
   traffic from the load balancer, and the timeout and threshold settings.
4. If the application fails the check (slow start, a dependency down), route it to the
   owning team.

## Warnings
Do not point the health check at a page that always returns 200 regardless of
application state; it hides real failures.

claims.claim: Ensure the security group allows traffic from the load balancer to the servers.

claims.claim: Check your employment terms to see if your role is office-based, hybrid, or fully remote.

cited.title: Working from home rules and exceptions
cited.text:
Working from home rules and exceptions (Workplace policy and reviews)
## Symptom
An employee asks how many days they must be in the office, or wants an exception to work
remotely for a period.

## Cause
Each role is office-based, hybrid or fully remote, as set in the employment terms. Hybrid
roles have a minimum number of office days per week set by the department.

## Resolution steps
1. Check the employee's role category in their employment terms.
2. For hybrid roles, the department's minimum office days apply.
3. Exceptions (for example temporary full remote for a personal reason) are requested from
   the manager, who decides with HR informed.
4. Equipment for home working is requested through the normal equipment request.

## Warnings
HR clarifies the policy; the manager approves individual exceptions.

Wrong date format in SAP

The dates in SAP are wrong, like 12/3 instead of 3/12. Also, numbers have commas instead of dots, like 1,000 for 1000. This makes the reports confusing and hard to read. Settings are supposed to match regional preferences, but not here. Need to fix this quickly for report generation.

claims.claim: Open transaction SU3 (own user data) and go to the Defaults tab.

cited.title: Wrong date or number format in SAP
cited.text:
Wrong date or number format in SAP (GUI, dumps and printing)
## Symptom
SAP shows dates as month/day/year instead of day/month/year, or uses a comma instead of a
decimal point, so amounts look ten or a thousand times wrong in downloads.

## Cause
Date and decimal formats are personal settings stored in the user's master record; they
may differ from Windows regional settings.

## Resolution steps
1. Open transaction SU3 (own user data) and go to the Defaults tab.
2. Choose the correct decimal notation and date format.
3. Save, then log off and log on again so the new settings apply.
4. Re-export any spreadsheet downloads made with the wrong format.

## Warnings
The formats affect only how values are displayed and exported, not the stored data; do
not correct postings because of a display format.

Goods movement posting failed

cited.title: Posting period closed for goods movements
cited.text:
Posting period closed for goods movements (Materials and number ranges)
## Symptom
A goods movement fails with a message that posting is only possible in two named
periods, for example the current and the previous month.

## Cause
The materials-management posting period only allows postings in the current and the
previous period. The period is moved forward each month with MMPV. If the month-end
change was not run, or the user picks a date in an older period, the posting is refused.

## Resolution steps

   periods named in the message, if that matches when the movement really happened.

   moved forward. Check the current period with MMRV.

   Finance, not the helpdesk.

drafts.ticket:
Vendor invoice blocked for payment

We received a query from a vendor regarding non-payment. The invoice was posted in MIRO, but it shows a payment block. This block happened despite the invoice being posted in MIRO. The payment run skipped this invoice, which is causing delays. It appears the block is due to a price variance beyond tolerances. Could you please investigate and resolve this issue?

claims.claim: Ask for the vendor number and invoice number.

cited.title: Vendor invoice blocked for payment
cited.text:
Vendor invoice blocked for payment (Purchasing and goods receipt)
## Symptom
A vendor says they have not been paid. The invoice was posted in MIRO but shows a
payment block, so the payment run skipped it.

## Cause
MIRO sets a payment block automatically when the invoice differs from the PO or the
goods receipt beyond the tolerances: usually a price variance, a quantity variance, or
an invoice posted before the goods receipt.

## Resolution steps
1. Ask for the vendor number and invoice number, and find the document.
2. Run MRBR (release blocked invoices) for that vendor to see why it is blocked: price,
   quantity or date variance.
3. For a quantity block caused by a missing goods receipt, ask the receiving team to post
   the receipt. The block can then be released.
4. For a price variance, the buyer must confirm the price with the vendor. If it is
   correct, accounts payable releases the invoice in MRBR.
5. Tell the vendor the invoice will be paid in the next payment run after release.

claims.claim: Run MRBR for the vendor to identify the reason for the block.

New app needs domain setup

Our new service is up but can't be accessed via the company domain. We need a DNS record for it and an HTTPS certificate. When can we get this done? Is there a specific name we should use for the domain? We need this soon for training sessions. Is there a specific name we should use for the domain?

claims.claim: Provide the desired domain name for the new service.

cited.title: New service needs a company domain name
cited.text:
New service needs a company domain name (Load balancers and certificates)
## Symptom
A team has a new application running behind a load balancer and wants it reachable under
a company domain name with HTTPS.

## Cause
The name needs a DNS record pointing at the load balancer and a certificate for that
name, both managed by the platform team.

## Resolution steps
1. Get the desired name, the load balancer, the environment and the owning team.
2. Request a certificate for the name; it is validated through a DNS record.
3. Ask the platform team to create an alias record that points the name at the load
   balancer.
4. Add the certificate to the load balancer's HTTPS listener and test the site with the
   new name.

## Warnings
Do not point records at a load balancer's IP addresses; they change. Use an alias record.

claims.claim: The platform team will create an alias DNS record pointing the domain at the load balancer.

I've checked the settings and added a few rules, but it's still not working. I've also tried restarting the firewall and the application, no luck. I'm not sure if I need a rule for the exact IP and port or if there's a generic rule I can use. We're losing productivity because of this delay. Can anyone help me with the firewall rule setup? Do we have a generic rule for such connections that I can apply temporarily until a custom rule is created?

claims.claim: Collect the source IP or subnet, destination IP or host, port numbers, and protocol (TCP or UDP) for the new application.

cited.title: Firewall rule needed for an application
cited.text:
Firewall rule needed for an application (Firewall and proxy)
## Symptom
A new application or integration cannot connect to a server or external service; the
connection times out because the firewall blocks it.

## Cause
The firewall denies traffic that no rule allows. A new connection needs a rule scoped to
the exact source, destination, port and protocol.

## Resolution steps
1. Collect source IP or subnet, destination IP or host, port numbers, protocol (TCP or
   UDP) and the business reason.
2. Raise a firewall change request through the change process; rules are never added ad
   hoc, even for urgent requests.
3. When the rule is in place, test with the requester, for example with
   `Test-NetConnection <host> -Port <port>` or the application's own connection test.
4. For temporary rules (a migration), record an end date so the rule is removed.

## Warnings
Never request or approve an any-to-any rule, even temporarily.

drafts.ticket:
Expired download link

Our team can't download the file. The link says 'Request has expired'. How long before we can get a new link? How often do we need to request new links for these files?

claims.claim: Contact the file owner to request a new download link.

cited.title: Shared download link to a bucket file has expired
cited.text:
Shared download link to a bucket file has expired (Object storage)
## Symptom
A partner or colleague opens a download link for a file in cloud storage and gets
"Request has expired" or access denied, although the link worked earlier.

## Cause
The link was a pre-signed URL. It works only for the lifetime set when it was created,
and never longer than the credentials used to sign it. Links signed with temporary role
credentials stop working when that session ends.

## Resolution steps
1. Confirm the link contains signature parameters (it is a pre-signed URL, not a public
   object).
2. Ask the file owner to generate a new link with an appropriate expiry.
3. For links that must last days, the owner should sign with credentials that remain
   valid for that long; the maximum lifetime is seven days.
4. For recurring sharing with a partner, recommend a proper partner-access setup instead
   of repeated links.

## Warnings
Do not make the object or bucket public to replace an expired link.

drafts.ticket:
IDoc status 51

Inbound IDoc WE02 shows status 51, no order created. Any ideas on next steps? Is there a specific timeout for these IDoc posts before they get stuck in status 51?

claims.claim: Open the IDoc in WE02 and read the status record for status 51.

cited.title: IDoc in status 51
cited.text:
IDoc in status 51 (Batch jobs and IDocs)
## Symptom
An inbound IDoc shows status 51, "Application document not posted", in WE02 or WE05,
and the expected order, delivery or invoice was never created.

## Cause
The IDoc arrived but the application could not post it. Typical reasons are missing
master data (customer, vendor or material), a missing pricing condition, or a partner
profile mismatch.

## Resolution steps
1. Open the IDoc in WE02 and read the status record for status 51. The error message
   usually names the missing field or master record.
2. Fix the cause, or ask the master-data team to create the missing record.
3. Reprocess the IDoc with BD87.
4. If many IDocs from the same partner fail at once, check the partner profile and any
   recent mapping change instead of fixing IDocs one by one.

## Warnings
Do not reprocess an IDoc repeatedly without reading the error. If the cause was
intermittent, repeated attempts can create duplicate documents.

claims.claim: The error message usually names the missing field or master record.

cited.title: Application cannot send email from the office network
cited.text:
Application cannot send email from the office network (Firewall and proxy)
## Symptom
A script, scanner or application that sends email directly fails to connect to the mail
server on port 25, while the same email account works in Outlook.

## Cause
Outbound SMTP on port 25 is blocked for all devices except the company mail relay, to
stop infected machines from sending spam.

## Resolution steps
1. Confirm what is sending the email: a device (scanner, printer) or an application.
2. Configure it to send through the internal mail relay, whose address is on the
   intranet, instead of an outside mail server.
3. If the relay needs to accept a new device, raise a request with the device's IP and
   the sender address it will use.

## Warnings
Do not request a firewall exception for port 25 to the internet.
