cited.title: Connected but no internet, 169.254 address
cited.text:
Connected but no internet, 169.254 address (DHCP and DNS)
## Symptom
The device connects to the network but shows "No internet" or "Limited", and
`ipconfig` shows an address starting with 169.254.

## Cause
A 169.254.x.x address is self-assigned when the device gets no reply from DHCP. One
device failing points to its cable, port or driver; many devices on the same network
point to the DHCP server or an exhausted address pool.

## Resolution steps
1. Disconnect and reconnect to trigger a new DHCP request.
2. Run `ipconfig /release` and then `ipconfig /renew`.
3. On a wired desk, try another cable and port.
4. If several devices on the same floor or network get 169.254 addresses, escalate to
   network engineering: the DHCP scope may be full or the server unreachable.

## Warnings
Do not give the device a static IP address as a fix; it can clash with addresses DHCP
hands out later.

cited.title: Internet slow for a whole floor
cited.text:
Internet slow for a whole floor (Call quality and file shares)
## Symptom
Many users on the same floor or office report that websites and cloud apps are slow at
the same time.

## Cause
A shared link or switch is saturated: a large download or backup, a faulty uplink running
at reduced speed, or the office internet link reaching capacity.

## Resolution steps
1. Confirm that several users in the same area are affected, and record when it started.
2. Ask whether anything unusual is running: large software deployments, backups or
   video events.
3. Escalate to network engineering with the location, the time and the number of users;
   they check link utilisation and uplink errors.
4. Keep the ticket open as a parent for the other users' reports.

## Warnings
Do not restart network equipment yourself.

cited.title: Posting period closed for goods movements
cited.text:
Posting period closed for goods movements (Materials and number ranges)
## Symptom
A goods movement fails with a message that posting is only possible in two named
periods, for example the current and the previous month.

## Cause
The materials-management posting period only allows postings in the current and the
previous period. The period is moved forward each month with MMPV. If the month-end
change was not run, or the user picks a date in an older period, the posting is refused.

## Resolution steps
1. Check the posting date the user entered. Ask them to use a date in one of the two
   periods named in the message, if that matches when the movement really happened.
2. If the current calendar month is not among the allowed periods, the period was not
   moved forward. Check the current period with MMRV.
3. Escalate a missing period change to the materials-management team, who run MMPV.
4. Postings into an older closed period need Finance approval and are handled by
   Finance, not the helpdesk.

claims.claim: Ensure it is within the current or previous month.

1. If the user works remotely, confirm the VPN is connected; see the Networking VPN
   articles if it is not.

   the server is probably down: escalate to Basis at once.
3. Check the system entry in SAP Logon: application server, instance number and system
   ID must match the values published by Basis. Entries can change after a system refresh.

   the instance number (3200 for instance 00).
5. If only this user is affected and the entry is correct, reinstall or update SAP GUI
   from the software centre.

cited.title: Internal names do not resolve
cited.text:
Internal names do not resolve (DHCP and DNS)
## Symptom
Public websites work, but internal names such as the intranet or a file server do not
open. The same resource opens when the user types its IP address.

## Cause
The device is not using the internal DNS servers: it is off the corporate network or VPN,
or it has public DNS servers set, which cannot resolve internal names.

## Resolution steps
1. Confirm the device is on the corporate network or connected to the VPN.
2. Run `ipconfig /all` and check that the DNS servers are the internal ones, not public
   resolvers such as 8.8.8.8.
3. If public DNS servers were set by hand, set the adapter back to obtain DNS
   automatically.
4. Run `ipconfig /flushdns` and retry.

## Warnings
Once the IP address works but the name does not, do not keep checking cables and Wi-Fi;
it is a DNS problem.

claims.claim: Run `ipconfig /all` and verify that the DNS servers are the internal ones.

ALTER TABLE hang blocks table

Our main table is stuck during an update. All queries are now timing out. Application reports database locks, but can't fix it. Tried increasing timeout, no luck. Users are complaining, and we need to fix. Need urgent assistance to resolve this.

claims.claim: Identify the session that is running the `ALTER TABLE` command with `SELECT * FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE query LIKE '%ALTER TABLE%';`.

cited.title: Schema change hangs and blocks the whole table
cited.text:
Schema change hangs and blocks the whole table (Locks and deadlocks)
## Symptom
An `ALTER TABLE` during a deployment hangs, and soon all queries on that table are blocked
too, causing an application outage.

## Cause
`ALTER TABLE` needs an exclusive lock. It waits behind any running transaction on the
table, and every new query then queues behind the waiting `ALTER TABLE`.

## Resolution steps
1. Cancel the waiting `ALTER TABLE` session to release the queue at once.
2. Find the long-running transaction it was waiting for.
3. Rerun the migration in a quiet window with a short `lock_timeout` (for example a few
   seconds), so it gives up instead of blocking everyone.
4. Retry the migration if it times out, rather than letting it wait.

## Warnings
Never run schema changes on busy tables without a lock timeout.

claims.claim: Cancel the `ALTER TABLE` session immediately to release the queue: `SELECT pg_cancel_backend(<session_id>);`.

cited.title: Queries blocked by an idle session holding a lock
cited.text:
Queries blocked by an idle session holding a lock (Locks and deadlocks)
## Symptom
Queries on a table hang waiting for a lock, and the session holding the lock is idle and
doing nothing.

## Cause
A session opened a transaction, took a lock, and then stopped without committing or
rolling back. It shows as "idle in transaction" and keeps its locks until it ends.

## Resolution steps
1. Find the blocking session with `pg_blocking_pids()` and `pg_stat_activity`.
2. Check its state and how long it has been idle in transaction.
3. Confirm with the owning application that the session is stuck, not a long legitimate job.
4. End it with `pg_terminate_backend(pid)`; its locks are released and waiting queries continue.
5. Ask the application team to close transactions on error paths.

## Warnings
Terminating a session rolls back its uncommitted work; confirm it is stuck first.

cited.title: Nightly database backup failed
cited.text:
Nightly database backup failed (Disk space and backups)
## Symptom
The backup monitoring reports that last night's backup of a database failed or did not run.

## Cause
Common causes are not enough space in the backup target, an expired credential for the
backup storage, a backup that overlapped a heavy batch job and timed out, or the
database being unreachable at the time.

## Resolution steps
1. Read the backup job's log for the exact error.
2. Fix the cause: free space or extend the target, renew the storage credential, or move
   the schedule away from the batch job.
3. Run an on-demand backup at once, so there is a recent good backup.
4. Confirm the new backup completed and its size is similar to previous ones.

## Warnings
A failed backup is not "fixed" until a new backup has completed successfully.

## Resolution steps
1. Confirm the internet works without the VPN by loading any public website.
2. Ask whether colleagues can connect. If several users fail at the same time, check the

Do not ask the user to turn off the Windows firewall or antivirus to test the VPN.

Goods receipt error in MIGO

MIGO blocks receipt when qty exceeds PO + tolerance. Over-delivery should be allowed within set limits. Tried adjusting tolerance but no luck. Unrelated: SAP UI keeps freezing during searches. Need admin intervention to resolve.

claims.claim: Check the PO in ME23N and note the ordered quantity, the quantity already received, and the over-delivery tolerance.

cited.title: Goods receipt quantity exceeds the PO quantity
cited.text:
Goods receipt quantity exceeds the PO quantity (Purchasing and goods receipt)
## Symptom
MIGO refuses the goods receipt because the quantity entered is larger than the open
quantity on the purchase order, even though the vendor really delivered that amount.

## Cause
Each PO item has an over-delivery tolerance (a percentage on the item's Delivery tab).
Receipts above the ordered quantity plus that tolerance are blocked, unless the item
allows unlimited over-delivery.

## Resolution steps
1. Display the PO in ME23N and note the ordered quantity, the quantity already received
   and the over-delivery tolerance on the item's Delivery tab.
2. Post a goods receipt for the quantity that is allowed (up to the tolerance) if the
   receiving team wants to accept that part now.
3. For the extra quantity, ask the buyer whether to accept it. If yes, the buyer
   increases the PO quantity in ME22N and the rest is received afterwards.
4. If the buyer does not accept the extra quantity, it is returned to the vendor.

drafts.ticket:
Database volume almost full

The monitoring tool keeps showing the database volume is almost full. I can't write new data; it's rejecting my inserts. Is there a threshold limit for disk usage that triggers this? How much space is left before the database stops accepting writes? How much space is left before the database stops accepting writes?

claims.claim: Check the `pg_wal` directory to see if it's large and causing the issue.

cited.title: Database disk almost full
cited.text:
Database disk almost full (Disk space and backups)
## Symptom
Monitoring warns the database volume is nearly full, or the database already rejects
writes because the disk is full.

## Cause
Table and index bloat, write-ahead log (WAL) files piling up because a replication slot
or WAL archiving is stuck, or genuine data growth.

## Resolution steps
1. Find what uses the space: data files, or the `pg_wal` directory.
2. If `pg_wal` is large, check `pg_replication_slots` for inactive slots and WAL archiving
   for failures.
3. If writes are already failing, expand the volume first to restore service.
4. Then fix the cause: remove an abandoned slot (after the DBA confirms), fix archiving,
   or address bloat.

## Warnings
Never delete files from `pg_wal` by hand; it can make the database impossible to start.

cited.title: WAL archiving failing
cited.text:
WAL archiving failing (Disk space and backups)
## Symptom
Monitoring reports WAL archive failures, and the `pg_wal` directory keeps growing.

## Cause
PostgreSQL keeps each WAL file until `archive_command` succeeds for it. If the archive
target is full, unreachable or its credentials expired, WAL files pile up locally.

## Resolution steps
1. Check `pg_stat_archiver` for `failed_count` and `last_failed_wal`.
2. Read the database log for the archive command's error message.
3. Fix the target: free space, restore network access, or renew the credential.
4. Confirm that archiving resumes and `pg_wal` shrinks as old files are archived.

## Warnings
Point-in-time recovery is broken while archiving fails; treat it as urgent.

claims.claim: Review `pg_replication_slots` for any inactive slots that might be taking up space.

MIRO payment block

Invoice posted but blocked. Checked PO and GR, but can’t resolve. Payment run skipped it today. How long does it usually take to unblock an invoice once the issue is identified and corrected?

claims.claim: Provide the vendor number and invoice number to the accounts payable team.

cited.title: Vendor invoice blocked for payment
cited.text:
Vendor invoice blocked for payment (Purchasing and goods receipt)
## Symptom
A vendor says they have not been paid. The invoice was posted in MIRO but shows a
payment block, so the payment run skipped it.

## Cause
MIRO sets a payment block automatically when the invoice differs from the PO or the
goods receipt beyond the tolerances: usually a price variance, a quantity variance, or
an invoice posted before the goods receipt.

## Resolution steps
1. Ask for the vendor number and invoice number, and find the document.
2. Run MRBR (release blocked invoices) for that vendor to see why it is blocked: price,
   quantity or date variance.
3. For a quantity block caused by a missing goods receipt, ask the receiving team to post
   the receipt. The block can then be released.
4. For a price variance, the buyer must confirm the price with the vendor. If it is
   correct, accounts payable releases the invoice in MRBR.
5. Tell the vendor the invoice will be paid in the next payment run after release.

Cloud console SSO issues

Can't log in via SSO. Got sent back to login page. Identity-provider error too. Or land on empty console with 'Access denied'. Checked passwords, still no luck. Same issue for other users too. Is there a deadline for resolving this issue by the end of the week?

cited.title: Single sign-on to the cloud console fails
cited.text:
Single sign-on to the cloud console fails (Identity, SSO and permissions)
## Symptom
The user cannot sign in to the cloud console through single sign-on: they are sent back to
the login page, see an identity-provider error, or land on an empty console with access
denied.

## Cause
The corporate account is locked or disabled, the user is not assigned to the cloud
application in the identity provider, or they are assigned but no role or permission set
is mapped to their group.

cited.title: Single sign-on to the cloud console fails
cited.text:
Single sign-on to the cloud console fails (Identity, SSO and permissions)
## Resolution steps
1. Ask whether other single sign-on apps work. If they all fail, it is an account problem
   in the identity provider, not a cloud problem.
2. Check that the user is assigned to the cloud console application in the identity
   provider. A missing assignment causes a redirect loop.
3. If sign-in works but the console is empty or denies everything, check which groups map
   to which cloud roles, and request the right group.
4. Ask the user to retry in a private browser window to rule out a stale session.
5. If many users fail at once, treat it as a single sign-on outage and escalate.

## Warnings
Do not create a local cloud user with a password as a workaround for single sign-on.

Video calls keep freezing

I use video calls for meetings every day. Sometimes the video or audio lags or freezes. It's not always the same call, but it happens often. When this happens, I can't see or hear properly. Web browsing is normal and not affected. I don't understand why it freezes, but it's annoying. It slows down my work, especially when I'm in a meeting. Is there a limit on the number of video calls allowed at the same time on our network?

claims.claim: Check if the issue happens on a cable connection instead of Wi-Fi.

cited.title: Video calls freeze or lag
cited.text:
Video calls freeze or lag (Call quality and file shares)
## Symptom
Video and audio calls freeze, drop or lag, while web browsing seems normal.

## Cause
Calls need low latency more than bandwidth. Weak Wi-Fi, large uploads on the same
connection, or VPN routing for a call that does not need it are the usual causes. If a
whole office is affected, the internet link is saturated.

## Resolution steps
1. Ask whether it happens on a cable too. If only on Wi-Fi, treat it as a Wi-Fi signal
   problem (move closer to an access point, or use a cable).
2. Check for large uploads or backups running at the same time.
3. If the user is on VPN for a call with outside participants, they can disconnect the VPN
   for the call.
4. Ask the user to run the call app's network test during a bad call and send the result.
5. If many users at one office are affected, escalate as a link-capacity problem.

## Warnings
Do not ask users to stop company backups to free bandwidth.

cited.title: Nightly database backup failed
cited.text:
Nightly database backup failed (Disk space and backups)
## Symptom
The backup monitoring reports that last night's backup of a database failed or did not run.

## Cause
Common causes are not enough space in the backup target, an expired credential for the
backup storage, a backup that overlapped a heavy batch job and timed out, or the
database being unreachable at the time.

## Resolution steps
1. Read the backup job's log for the exact error.
2. Fix the cause: free space or extend the target, renew the storage credential, or move
   the schedule away from the batch job.
3. Run an on-demand backup at once, so there is a recent good backup.
4. Confirm the new backup completed and its size is similar to previous ones.

## Warnings
A failed backup is not "fixed" until a new backup has completed successfully.

cited.title: WAL archiving failing
cited.text:
WAL archiving failing (Disk space and backups)
## Symptom
Monitoring reports WAL archive failures, and the `pg_wal` directory keeps growing.

## Cause
PostgreSQL keeps each WAL file until `archive_command` succeeds for it. If the archive
target is full, unreachable or its credentials expired, WAL files pile up locally.

## Resolution steps
1. Check `pg_stat_archiver` for `failed_count` and `last_failed_wal`.
2. Read the database log for the archive command's error message.
3. Fix the target: free space, restore network access, or renew the credential.
4. Confirm that archiving resumes and `pg_wal` shrinks as old files are archived.

## Warnings
Point-in-time recovery is broken while archiving fails; treat it as urgent.

claims.claim: Ensure the database is not under heavy load or experiencing any other performance issues that might prevent automatic failover.

cited.title: Nightly database backup failed
cited.text:
Nightly database backup failed (Disk space and backups)
## Symptom
The backup monitoring reports that last night's backup of a database failed or did not run.

## Cause
Common causes are not enough space in the backup target, an expired credential for the
backup storage, a backup that overlapped a heavy batch job and timed out, or the
database being unreachable at the time.

## Resolution steps
1. Read the backup job's log for the exact error.
2. Fix the cause: free space or extend the target, renew the storage credential, or move
   the schedule away from the batch job.
3. Run an on-demand backup at once, so there is a recent good backup.
4. Confirm the new backup completed and its size is similar to previous ones.

## Warnings
A failed backup is not "fixed" until a new backup has completed successfully.

cited.title: Statement cancelled due to statement or lock timeout
cited.text:
Statement cancelled due to statement or lock timeout (Locks and deadlocks)
## Symptom
A query fails with "canceling statement due to statement timeout" or "canceling statement
due to lock timeout".

## Cause
The database cancels statements that run longer than `statement_timeout`, or wait for a
lock longer than `lock_timeout`. These limits protect the database from runaway queries
and long lock queues.

## Resolution steps
1. Note which message appeared: statement timeout means the query ran too long; lock
   timeout means it waited too long for another session.
2. For a statement timeout, get the query and analyse it (see the slow query article).
3. For a lock timeout, find what held the lock at that time, usually a long transaction
   or a migration.
4. If a specific report legitimately needs longer, the owning team can set a higher
   timeout for that session only.

## Warnings
Do not raise the timeout for the whole database to make one query pass.

Posting period closed for goods movements (Materials and number ranges)
## Symptom
A goods movement fails with a message that posting is only possible in two named
periods, for example the current and the previous month.

## Cause
The materials-management posting period only allows postings in the current and the
previous period. The period is moved forward each month with MMPV. If the month-end
change was not run, or the user picks a date in an older period, the posting is refused.

## Resolution steps
1. Check the posting date the user entered. Ask them to use a date in one of the two
   periods named in the message, if that matches when the movement really happened.

   moved forward. Check the current period with MMRV.
3. Escalate a missing period change to the materials-management team, who run MMPV.
4. Postings into an older closed period need Finance approval and are handled by
   Finance, not the helpdesk.

cited.title: Internet slow for a whole floor
cited.text:
Internet slow for a whole floor (Call quality and file shares)
## Symptom
Many users on the same floor or office report that websites and cloud apps are slow at
the same time.

## Cause
A shared link or switch is saturated: a large download or backup, a faulty uplink running
at reduced speed, or the office internet link reaching capacity.

## Resolution steps
1. Confirm that several users in the same area are affected, and record when it started.
2. Ask whether anything unusual is running: large software deployments, backups or
   video events.
3. Escalate to network engineering with the location, the time and the number of users;
   they check link utilisation and uplink errors.
4. Keep the ticket open as a parent for the other users' reports.

## Warnings
Do not restart network equipment yourself.

cited.title: Video calls freeze or lag
cited.text:
Video calls freeze or lag (Call quality and file shares)
## Symptom
Video and audio calls freeze, drop or lag, while web browsing seems normal.

## Cause
Calls need low latency more than bandwidth. Weak Wi-Fi, large uploads on the same
connection, or VPN routing for a call that does not need it are the usual causes. If a
whole office is affected, the internet link is saturated.

## Resolution steps
1. Ask whether it happens on a cable too. If only on Wi-Fi, treat it as a Wi-Fi signal
   problem (move closer to an access point, or use a cable).
2. Check for large uploads or backups running at the same time.
3. If the user is on VPN for a call with outside participants, they can disconnect the VPN
   for the call.
4. Ask the user to run the call app's network test during a bad call and send the result.
5. If many users at one office are affected, escalate as a link-capacity problem.

## Warnings
Do not ask users to stop company backups to free bandwidth.

cited.title: Office Wi-Fi keeps dropping
cited.text:
Office Wi-Fi keeps dropping (Wireless access)
## Symptom
A laptop repeatedly disconnects from the office Wi-Fi, especially after being idle or
when the user moves between meeting rooms.

## Cause
Most often the adapter's power saving turns the radio down when idle, or the laptop holds
on to a distant access point. When many users in one area drop at once, an access point
or the wireless controller is at fault.

## Resolution steps
1. Ask whether colleagues in the same area are affected. If yes, record the location and
   escalate it as an access point problem.
2. Note the network name and the access point the laptop was last connected to, from the
   connection details.
3. Forget the network and reconnect to clear a stale saved profile.
4. Set the adapter's power management so Windows cannot turn it off to save power, and
   update the wireless driver from the software centre.

## Warnings
Do not tell users to connect to the guest network instead; it has no access to internal
systems.

Today's reports are taking unusually long to generate. Some queries are timing out, but not all. The database seems sluggish, affecting multiple tables. This isn't consistent across all tables or queries. Something feels off, but I can't pipnoint the exact problem.

cited.title: Database server CPU is very high
cited.text:
Database server CPU is very high (Query performance and indexes)
## Symptom
Monitoring shows the database server's CPU near 100 percent and applications are slow.

## Cause
A few expensive queries usually cause most of the load: a new query without a suitable
index, a report run at peak time, or a query whose plan changed after data growth.

## Resolution steps
1. Look at `pg_stat_activity` for long-running active queries right now.
2. Check `pg_stat_statements` for the queries with the highest total execution time.
3. If one report or job causes the spike, ask its owner to stop it or run it off-peak.
4. Send the top queries and their plans to the owning teams for tuning.

## Warnings
Do not restart the database to clear CPU load; it drops every connection and the load
usually returns.

claims.claim: Review `pg_stat_statements` for the queries with the highest execution time.

SAP date & number format issues

SAP displays dates as 04/05/2023 instead of 05/04/2023. Amounts in downloads appear incorrect with commas as decimals. Settings are personal, independent of Windows regional config. Affects financial reporting and daily transactions accuracy. Need urgent change to standard formats for consistency.

claims.claim: Open transaction SU3 (own user data) and go to the Defaults tab.

cited.title: Wrong date or number format in SAP
cited.text:
Wrong date or number format in SAP (GUI, dumps and printing)
## Symptom
SAP shows dates as month/day/year instead of day/month/year, or uses a comma instead of a
decimal point, so amounts look ten or a thousand times wrong in downloads.

## Cause
Date and decimal formats are personal settings stored in the user's master record; they
may differ from Windows regional settings.

## Resolution steps
1. Open transaction SU3 (own user data) and go to the Defaults tab.
2. Choose the correct decimal notation and date format.
3. Save, then log off and log on again so the new settings apply.
4. Re-export any spreadsheet downloads made with the wrong format.

## Warnings
The formats affect only how values are displayed and exported, not the stored data; do
not correct postings because of a display format.

drafts.ticket:
Table size keeps growing

Our table's disk usage is increasing, despite regular row deletions. Queries are getting slower, and the autovacuum seems not to be working. Need help to figure out why rows aren't being properly cleaned up.

claims.claim: Check the `n_dead_tup` and `last_autovacuum` for the table in `pg_stat_user_tables`.

cited.title: Table keeps growing although rows are deleted
cited.text:
Table keeps growing although rows are deleted (Query performance and indexes)
## Symptom
A table's size on disk keeps growing and queries on it get slower, even though the
application deletes or updates old rows regularly.

## Cause
Updates and deletes leave dead row versions. Autovacuum normally cleans them so the space
can be reused. If autovacuum cannot keep up, or a long-running transaction stops it from
removing dead rows, the table bloats.

## Resolution steps
1. Check `n_dead_tup` and `last_autovacuum` for the table in `pg_stat_user_tables`.
2. Look for long-running or idle-in-transaction sessions in `pg_stat_activity`; they block
   cleanup.
3. Once those sessions end, run `VACUUM (ANALYZE)` on the table.
4. If autovacuum regularly falls behind on this table, ask the DBA team to tune its
   autovacuum settings.

## Warnings
`VACUUM FULL` rewrites the table under an exclusive lock; never run it on a busy table
without a maintenance window.

Goods movement posting error

I'm getting an error that says the posting period is closed for this goods movement. It seems to be restricted to only the current and previous periods, but I'm not sure why it's not working today.

claims.claim: Check the posting date you entered.

cited.title: Posting period closed for goods movements
cited.text:
Posting period closed for goods movements (Materials and number ranges)
## Symptom
A goods movement fails with a message that posting is only possible in two named
periods, for example the current and the previous month.

## Cause
The materials-management posting period only allows postings in the current and the
previous period. The period is moved forward each month with MMPV. If the month-end
change was not run, or the user picks a date in an older period, the posting is refused.

## Resolution steps
1. Check the posting date the user entered. Ask them to use a date in one of the two
   periods named in the message, if that matches when the movement really happened.
2. If the current calendar month is not among the allowed periods, the period was not
   moved forward. Check the current period with MMRV.
3. Escalate a missing period change to the materials-management team, who run MMPV.
4. Postings into an older closed period need Finance approval and are handled by
   Finance, not the helpdesk.

drafts.ticket:
Number range exhausted

Just tried to create a new material document, got 'no number available.' Checked the SAP log; seems like the last number was used. Tried reassigning numbers but got the same error. Restarted my computer, no luck. Number ranges were set up laast year; no updates since then. Colleague had similar issue yesterday; we both work in the same project. Is there a limit to how many documents can be created in a fiscal year? Is there a limit to how many documents can be created in a fiscal year?

claims.claim: Check if the issue started at the beginning of a fiscal year.

cited.title: Number range exhausted
cited.text:
Number range exhausted (Materials and number ranges)
## Symptom
Creating a document (material, purchase order, sales order or accounting document) fails
because no number can be assigned: the message says the number range interval is full or
was not found.

## Cause
Every document type draws its numbers from a number range interval. When the interval
reaches its upper limit, or the interval for a new fiscal year was never created, no new
documents of that type can be saved.

## Resolution steps
1. Note the exact message, the document type and the company code or plant.
2. Identify the number range object (for example FBN1 for accounting documents, MMNR for
   materials, or SNRO for the generic view).
3. Escalate to the SAP configuration team with the object, the interval and the fiscal
   year. Extending or adding an interval is a configuration change.
4. If the error appeared at the start of a fiscal year, mention it: the new year's
   interval may simply not have been created.

cited.title: IDoc in status 51
cited.text:
IDoc in status 51 (Batch jobs and IDocs)
## Symptom
An inbound IDoc shows status 51, "Application document not posted", in WE02 or WE05,
and the expected order, delivery or invoice was never created.

## Cause
The IDoc arrived but the application could not post it. Typical reasons are missing
master data (customer, vendor or material), a missing pricing condition, or a partner
profile mismatch.

## Resolution steps
1. Open the IDoc in WE02 and read the status record for status 51. The error message
   usually names the missing field or master record.
2. Fix the cause, or ask the master-data team to create the missing record.
3. Reprocess the IDoc with BD87.
4. If many IDocs from the same partner fail at once, check the partner profile and any
   recent mapping change instead of fixing IDocs one by one.

## Warnings
Do not reprocess an IDoc repeatedly without reading the error. If the cause was
intermittent, repeated attempts can create duplicate documents.

cited.title: Material master locked by another user
cited.text:
Material master locked by another user (Materials and number ranges)
## Symptom
Changing a material in MM02 fails with a message that the material is currently being
processed by another user, who is named in the message.

## Cause
SAP sets a lock entry while someone edits a material. The lock is released when they
save or leave the transaction. If their session crashed, the lock can be left behind.

## Resolution steps
1. Contact the named user and ask them to save or exit MM02. This releases the lock at once.
2. If they are unreachable or say they are not editing, check SM12 for the lock entry on
   the material and note the user and the time it was created.
3. A Basis administrator confirms the user has no active session (SM04) before deleting
   the lock entry in SM12.
4. Ask the original requester to retry MM02.

## Warnings
Deleting a lock entry while the other user is still editing can corrupt the material
data. Only Basis deletes lock entries, and only after confirming the session is gone.

claims.claim: If a colleague is editing, ask them to save or exit the transaction.

cited.title: Wi-Fi access for a visitor
cited.text:
Wi-Fi access for a visitor (Wireless access)
## Symptom
An employee asks for internet access for a visitor, contractor or vendor who is on site.

## Cause
Visitors may not join the corporate network. Guest access is a separate, isolated network

cited.title: Internal names do not resolve
cited.text:
Internal names do not resolve (DHCP and DNS)
## Symptom
Public websites work, but internal names such as the intranet or a file server do not
open. The same resource opens when the user types its IP address.

## Cause
The device is not using the internal DNS servers: it is off the corporate network or VPN,
or it has public DNS servers set, which cannot resolve internal names.

## Resolution steps
1. Confirm the device is on the corporate network or connected to the VPN.
2. Run `ipconfig /all` and check that the DNS servers are the internal ones, not public
   resolvers such as 8.8.8.8.
3. If public DNS servers were set by hand, set the adapter back to obtain DNS
   automatically.
4. Run `ipconfig /flushdns` and retry.

## Warnings
Once the IP address works but the name does not, do not keep checking cables and Wi-Fi;
it is a DNS problem.

cited.title: VPN connected but internal sites do not open
cited.text:
VPN connected but internal sites do not open (VPN connectivity)
## Symptom
The VPN client says it is connected, but internal websites, file shares and SAP do not
open. Public websites still work.

## Cause
The VPN tunnel is up but the laptop is not using the internal DNS servers pushed by the
VPN, or a home router uses the same private address range as an internal network, so
traffic for that range never enters the tunnel.

## Resolution steps
1. Ask the user to try an internal resource by IP address. If the IP works but the name
   does not, it is a DNS problem.
2. Run `ipconfig /all` and check that the VPN adapter lists the internal DNS servers.
3. Disconnect and reconnect the VPN; if DNS is still wrong, reinstall the VPN profile from
   the software centre.
4. If even IP addresses fail, compare the home network's address range with the internal
   ranges (for example both using 192.168.1.x). Ask the user to restart the home router
   or test from a hotspot, and report the overlap to network engineering.

cited.title: Office Wi-Fi keeps dropping
cited.text:
Office Wi-Fi keeps dropping (Wireless access)
## Symptom
A laptop repeatedly disconnects from the office Wi-Fi, especially after being idle or
when the user moves between meeting rooms.

## Cause
Most often the adapter's power saving turns the radio down when idle, or the laptop holds
on to a distant access point. When many users in one area drop at once, an access point
or the wireless controller is at fault.

## Resolution steps
1. Ask whether colleagues in the same area are affected. If yes, record the location and
   escalate it as an access point problem.
2. Note the network name and the access point the laptop was last connected to, from the
   connection details.
3. Forget the network and reconnect to clear a stale saved profile.
4. Set the adapter's power management so Windows cannot turn it off to save power, and
   update the wireless driver from the software centre.

## Warnings
Do not tell users to connect to the guest network instead; it has no access to internal
systems.

cited.title: Connected but no internet, 169.254 address
cited.text:
Connected but no internet, 169.254 address (DHCP and DNS)
## Symptom
The device connects to the network but shows "No internet" or "Limited", and
`ipconfig` shows an address starting with 169.254.

## Cause
A 169.254.x.x address is self-assigned when the device gets no reply from DHCP. One
device failing points to its cable, port or driver; many devices on the same network
point to the DHCP server or an exhausted address pool.

## Resolution steps
1. Disconnect and reconnect to trigger a new DHCP request.
2. Run `ipconfig /release` and then `ipconfig /renew`.
3. On a wired desk, try another cable and port.
4. If several devices on the same floor or network get 169.254 addresses, escalate to
   network engineering: the DHCP scope may be full or the server unreachable.

## Warnings
Do not give the device a static IP address as a fix; it can clash with addresses DHCP
hands out later.

cited.title: Windows reports an IP address conflict
cited.text:
Windows reports an IP address conflict (DHCP and DNS)
## Symptom
Windows shows "Windows has detected an IP address conflict" and the connection becomes
unreliable or drops.

## Cause
Two devices are using the same IP address, almost always because one of them (a printer,
a test machine) was given a static address inside the DHCP range.

## Resolution steps
1. Run `ipconfig /release` and `ipconfig /renew` on the user's laptop to get a new
   address; this usually restores the connection at once.
2. Note the conflicting address from the message or the event log.
3. Report the address to network engineering so they can find the device with the static
   address and either reserve it or move it outside the DHCP range.

## Warnings
Do not set a static address on the laptop to escape the conflict; it only moves the
problem.

cited.title: Office Wi-Fi keeps dropping
cited.text:
Office Wi-Fi keeps dropping (Wireless access)
## Symptom
A laptop repeatedly disconnects from the office Wi-Fi, especially after being idle or
when the user moves between meeting rooms.

## Cause
Most often the adapter's power saving turns the radio down when idle, or the laptop holds
on to a distant access point. When many users in one area drop at once, an access point
or the wireless controller is at fault.

## Resolution steps
1. Ask whether colleagues in the same area are affected. If yes, record the location and
   escalate it as an access point problem.
2. Note the network name and the access point the laptop was last connected to, from the
   connection details.
3. Forget the network and reconnect to clear a stale saved profile.
4. Set the adapter's power management so Windows cannot turn it off to save power, and
   update the wireless driver from the software centre.

## Warnings
Do not tell users to connect to the guest network instead; it has no access to internal
systems.

cited.title: VPN connected but internal sites do not open
cited.text:
VPN connected but internal sites do not open (VPN connectivity)
## Symptom
The VPN client says it is connected, but internal websites, file shares and SAP do not
open. Public websites still work.

## Cause
The VPN tunnel is up but the laptop is not using the internal DNS servers pushed by the
VPN, or a home router uses the same private address range as an internal network, so
traffic for that range never enters the tunnel.

## Resolution steps
1. Ask the user to try an internal resource by IP address. If the IP works but the name
   does not, it is a DNS problem.
2. Run `ipconfig /all` and check that the VPN adapter lists the internal DNS servers.
3. Disconnect and reconnect the VPN; if DNS is still wrong, reinstall the VPN profile from
   the software centre.
4. If even IP addresses fail, compare the home network's address range with the internal
   ranges (for example both using 192.168.1.x). Ask the user to restart the home router
   or test from a hotspot, and report the overlap to network engineering.

cited.title: Connected but no internet, 169.254 address
cited.text:
Connected but no internet, 169.254 address (DHCP and DNS)
## Symptom
The device connects to the network but shows "No internet" or "Limited", and
`ipconfig` shows an address starting with 169.254.

## Cause
A 169.254.x.x address is self-assigned when the device gets no reply from DHCP. One
device failing points to its cable, port or driver; many devices on the same network
point to the DHCP server or an exhausted address pool.

## Resolution steps
1. Disconnect and reconnect to trigger a new DHCP request.
2. Run `ipconfig /release` and then `ipconfig /renew`.
3. On a wired desk, try another cable and port.
4. If several devices on the same floor or network get 169.254 addresses, escalate to
   network engineering: the DHCP scope may be full or the server unreachable.

## Warnings
Do not give the device a static IP address as a fix; it can clash with addresses DHCP
hands out later.

cited.title: Internal names do not resolve
cited.text:
Internal names do not resolve (DHCP and DNS)
## Symptom
Public websites work, but internal names such as the intranet or a file server do not
open. The same resource opens when the user types its IP address.

## Cause
The device is not using the internal DNS servers: it is off the corporate network or VPN,
or it has public DNS servers set, which cannot resolve internal names.

## Resolution steps
1. Confirm the device is on the corporate network or connected to the VPN.
2. Run `ipconfig /all` and check that the DNS servers are the internal ones, not public
   resolvers such as 8.8.8.8.
3. If public DNS servers were set by hand, set the adapter back to obtain DNS
   automatically.
4. Run `ipconfig /flushdns` and retry.

## Warnings
Once the IP address works but the name does not, do not keep checking cables and Wi-Fi;
it is a DNS problem.

cited.title: Windows reports an IP address conflict
cited.text:
Windows reports an IP address conflict (DHCP and DNS)
## Symptom
Windows shows "Windows has detected an IP address conflict" and the connection becomes
unreliable or drops.

## Cause
Two devices are using the same IP address, almost always because one of them (a printer,
a test machine) was given a static address inside the DHCP range.

## Resolution steps
1. Run `ipconfig /release` and `ipconfig /renew` on the user's laptop to get a new
   address; this usually restores the connection at once.
2. Note the conflicting address from the message or the event log.
3. Report the address to network engineering so they can find the device with the static
   address and either reserve it or move it outside the DHCP range.

## Warnings
Do not set a static address on the laptop to escape the conflict; it only moves the
problem.

Posting period closed for goods movements (Materials and number ranges)
## Symptom
A goods movement fails with a message that posting is only possible in two named
periods, for example the current and the previous month.

## Cause
The materials-management posting period only allows postings in the current and the
previous period. The period is moved forward each month with MMPV. If the month-end
change was not run, or the user picks a date in an older period, the posting is refused.

## Resolution steps
1. Check the posting date the user entered. Ask them to use a date in one of the two
   periods named in the message, if that matches when the movement really happened.

   moved forward. Check the current period with MMRV.
3. Escalate a missing period change to the materials-management team, who run MMPV.
4. Postings into an older closed period need Finance approval and are handled by
   Finance, not the helpdesk.

cited.title: Database server CPU is very high
cited.text:
Database server CPU is very high (Query performance and indexes)
## Symptom
Monitoring shows the database server's CPU near 100 percent and applications are slow.

## Cause
A few expensive queries usually cause most of the load: a new query without a suitable
index, a report run at peak time, or a query whose plan changed after data growth.

## Resolution steps
1. Look at `pg_stat_activity` for long-running active queries right now.
2. Check `pg_stat_statements` for the queries with the highest total execution time.
3. If one report or job causes the spike, ask its owner to stop it or run it off-peak.
4. Send the top queries and their plans to the owning teams for tuning.

## Warnings
Do not restart the database to clear CPU load; it drops every connection and the load
usually returns.

cited.title: Queries blocked by an idle session holding a lock
cited.text:
Queries blocked by an idle session holding a lock (Locks and deadlocks)
## Symptom
Queries on a table hang waiting for a lock, and the session holding the lock is idle and
doing nothing.

## Cause
A session opened a transaction, took a lock, and then stopped without committing or
rolling back. It shows as "idle in transaction" and keeps its locks until it ends.

## Resolution steps
1. Find the blocking session with `pg_blocking_pids()` and `pg_stat_activity`.
2. Check its state and how long it has been idle in transaction.
3. Confirm with the owning application that the session is stuck, not a long legitimate job.
4. End it with `pg_terminate_backend(pid)`; its locks are released and waiting queries continue.
5. Ask the application team to close transactions on error paths.

## Warnings
Terminating a session rolls back its uncommitted work; confirm it is stuck first.

claims.claim: Confirm with the application team that the idle session is stuck and terminate it if necessary.

cited.title: Statement cancelled due to statement or lock timeout
cited.text:
Statement cancelled due to statement or lock timeout (Locks and deadlocks)
## Symptom
A query fails with "canceling statement due to statement timeout" or "canceling statement
due to lock timeout".

## Cause
The database cancels statements that run longer than `statement_timeout`, or wait for a
lock longer than `lock_timeout`. These limits protect the database from runaway queries
and long lock queues.

## Resolution steps
1. Note which message appeared: statement timeout means the query ran too long; lock
   timeout means it waited too long for another session.
2. For a statement timeout, get the query and analyse it (see the slow query article).
3. For a lock timeout, find what held the lock at that time, usually a long transaction
   or a migration.
4. If a specific report legitimately needs longer, the owning team can set a higher
   timeout for that session only.

## Warnings
Do not raise the timeout for the whole database to make one query pass.

claims.claim: If a query is timing out, analyze the query and consider setting a higher `statement_timeout` if it's a legitimate long-running job.

cited.title: Statement cancelled due to statement or lock timeout

## Symptom

due to lock timeout".

## Cause
The database cancels statements that run longer than `statement_timeout`, or wait for a
lock longer than `lock_timeout`. These limits protect the database from runaway queries
and long lock queues.

## Resolution steps
1. Note which message appeared: statement timeout means the query ran too long; lock

2. For a statement timeout, get the query and analyse it (see the slow query article).
3. For a lock timeout, find what held the lock at that time, usually a long transaction

4. If a specific report legitimately needs longer, the owning team can set a higher

Do not raise the timeout for the whole database to make one query pass.

claims.claim: If a query is waiting for a lock, identify the transaction holding the lock and consider rerunning the migration with a shorter `lock_timeout`.

cited.title: Schema change hangs and blocks the whole table
cited.text:
Schema change hangs and blocks the whole table (Locks and deadlocks)
## Symptom
An `ALTER TABLE` during a deployment hangs, and soon all queries on that table are blocked
too, causing an application outage.

## Cause
`ALTER TABLE` needs an exclusive lock. It waits behind any running transaction on the
table, and every new query then queues behind the waiting `ALTER TABLE`.

## Resolution steps
1. Cancel the waiting `ALTER TABLE` session to release the queue at once.
2. Find the long-running transaction it was waiting for.
3. Rerun the migration in a quiet window with a short `lock_timeout` (for example a few
   seconds), so it gives up instead of blocking everyone.
4. Retry the migration if it times out, rather than letting it wait.

## Warnings
Never run schema changes on busy tables without a lock timeout.

cited.text:
Adding a family member to health insurance (Benefits and insurance)
## Symptom
An employee wants to add a spouse, partner or child to their health insurance.

## Cause
Dependants can be added only within 30 days of becoming eligible (marriage, birth,

arrears back to the coverage start date.

Just had another call freeze mid-conference. Tried rebooting my PC and router, no change. Browsing websites works fine, only calls lag. Even with low Wi-Fi signal, others can stream fine. Calls from home work well, so it’s likely local issue here. Team meetings are increasingly interrupted by freezing. Need a stable call for next project presentation.

cited.title: Video calls freeze or lag
cited.text:
Video calls freeze or lag (Call quality and file shares)
## Symptom
Video and audio calls freeze, drop or lag, while web browsing seems normal.

## Cause
Calls need low latency more than bandwidth. Weak Wi-Fi, large uploads on the same
connection, or VPN routing for a call that does not need it are the usual causes. If a
whole office is affected, the internet link is saturated.

## Resolution steps
1. Ask whether it happens on a cable too. If only on Wi-Fi, treat it as a Wi-Fi signal
   problem (move closer to an access point, or use a cable).
2. Check for large uploads or backups running at the same time.
3. If the user is on VPN for a call with outside participants, they can disconnect the VPN
   for the call.
4. Ask the user to run the call app's network test during a bad call and send the result.
5. If many users at one office are affected, escalate as a link-capacity problem.

## Warnings
Do not ask users to stop company backups to free bandwidth.

Number range exhausted

Can't create new documents. Message says number range full or missing. Affects material, PO, SO, and accounting docs.

claims.claim: Note the exact message, document type, and company code or plant.

cited.title: Number range exhausted
cited.text:
Number range exhausted (Materials and number ranges)
## Symptom
Creating a document (material, purchase order, sales order or accounting document) fails
because no number can be assigned: the message says the number range interval is full or
was not found.

## Cause
Every document type draws its numbers from a number range interval. When the interval
reaches its upper limit, or the interval for a new fiscal year was never created, no new
documents of that type can be saved.

## Resolution steps
1. Note the exact message, the document type and the company code or plant.
2. Identify the number range object (for example FBN1 for accounting documents, MMNR for
   materials, or SNRO for the generic view).
3. Escalate to the SAP configuration team with the object, the interval and the fiscal
   year. Extending or adding an interval is a configuration change.
4. If the error appeared at the start of a fiscal year, mention it: the new year's
   interval may simply not have been created.

Number range exhausted (Materials and number ranges)
## Symptom
Creating a document (material, purchase order, sales order or accounting document) fails
because no number can be assigned: the message says the number range interval is full or
was not found.

## Cause
Every document type draws its numbers from a number range interval. When the interval
reaches its upper limit, or the interval for a new fiscal year was never created, no new

   year. Extending or adding an interval is a configuration change.

   interval may simply not have been created.

## Symptom
An employee asks how to file a health insurance claim, or why one is still not paid.

Claims are processed by the insurance carrier, not by HR. In-network providers file

drafts.ticket:
Queries waiting for lock

Our critical report queries are hanging, waiting for a lock held by an idle session. How long can this idle session keep the lock before it's forced to commit or rollback? How long can this idle session keep the lock before it's forced to commit or rollback?

claims.claim: Identify the idle session holding the lock using `pg_blocking_pids()` and `pg_stat_activity`.

cited.title: Queries blocked by an idle session holding a lock
cited.text:
Queries blocked by an idle session holding a lock (Locks and deadlocks)
## Symptom
Queries on a table hang waiting for a lock, and the session holding the lock is idle and
doing nothing.

## Cause
A session opened a transaction, took a lock, and then stopped without committing or
rolling back. It shows as "idle in transaction" and keeps its locks until it ends.

## Resolution steps
1. Find the blocking session with `pg_blocking_pids()` and `pg_stat_activity`.
2. Check its state and how long it has been idle in transaction.
3. Confirm with the owning application that the session is stuck, not a long legitimate job.
4. End it with `pg_terminate_backend(pid)`; its locks are released and waiting queries continue.
5. Ask the application team to close transactions on error paths.

## Warnings
Terminating a session rolls back its uncommitted work; confirm it is stuck first.

claims.claim: Check the state of the session and how long it has been idle in transaction.

cited.title: Request to run a data fix in production
cited.text:
Request to run a data fix in production (Access requests and schema changes)
## Symptom
A team asks the DBA team to run an `UPDATE` or `DELETE` script in production to correct
bad data.

## Cause
Application bugs or bad imports leave wrong data that the application cannot correct
itself.

## Resolution steps
1. Require the script, the expected number of affected rows and an approved change request.
2. Run the script's `WHERE` clause as a `SELECT COUNT(*)` first and compare with the
   expected number.
3. Take a backup of the affected rows (or an on-demand backup) before running it.
4. Run the script in a transaction, check the row count reported, and only then commit.

## Warnings
Never run a data fix that has no `WHERE` clause or whose row count does not match the
expected number.

cited.title: Password authentication failed after credential rotation
cited.text:
Password authentication failed after credential rotation (Connections and pools)
## Symptom
An application suddenly fails with "password authentication failed for user" after a
scheduled credential rotation, while other applications work.

## Cause
The database password was rotated in the secrets manager, but this application still uses
the old password: it caches it at start-up, or reads it from a configuration file instead
of the secrets manager.

## Resolution steps
1. Confirm the failing user name and the time the errors began; compare with the rotation
   time.
2. Check how the application gets its password: secrets manager or configuration file.
3. If it uses the secrets manager but caches the value, restart the application so it
   reads the new password.
4. If it uses a configuration file, ask the owning team to switch to the secrets manager.

## Warnings
Do not reset the database password back to the old value; other applications already use
the new one.

claims.claim: Restart the application to release any leaked database connections and check if the issue persists.

cited.title: Application runs out of database connections
cited.text:
Application runs out of database connections (Connections and pools)
## Symptom
Application logs show "connection pool exhausted", "sorry, too many clients already", or
requests waiting for a database connection, while the database server is up.

## Cause
Either the database reached `max_connections`, or the application's pool is full because
code paths take connections and never return them (a leak), often after an unhandled
error. Sessions left "idle in transaction" also hold connection slots.

## Resolution steps
1. Compare the number of connections in `pg_stat_activity` with `SHOW max_connections`.
2. Group the sessions by application and state; many "idle in transaction" sessions from
   one application point to that application.
3. Check whether the errors started after a deployment; a new code path that does not
   close its connection is the usual cause.
4. As a stop-gap, restart the affected application instance to release leaked connections.
5. Send the findings to the owning team to fix the leak or pool settings.

## Warnings
Raising `max_connections` hides a leak and costs memory on the server; fix the leak first.

cited.title: Posting period closed for goods movements
cited.text:
Posting period closed for goods movements (Materials and number ranges)
## Symptom
A goods movement fails with a message that posting is only possible in two named
periods, for example the current and the previous month.

## Cause
The materials-management posting period only allows postings in the current and the
previous period. The period is moved forward each month with MMPV. If the month-end
change was not run, or the user picks a date in an older period, the posting is refused.

## Resolution steps
1. Check the posting date the user entered. Ask them to use a date in one of the two
   periods named in the message, if that matches when the movement really happened.
2. If the current calendar month is not among the allowed periods, the period was not
   moved forward. Check the current period with MMRV.
3. Escalate a missing period change to the materials-management team, who run MMPV.
4. Postings into an older closed period need Finance approval and are handled by
   Finance, not the helpdesk.

claims.claim: Ensure it is within the current or previous month.

A goods movement fails with a message that posting is only possible in two named
periods, for example the current and the previous month.

## Cause
The materials-management posting period only allows postings in the current and the
previous period. The period is moved forward each month with MMPV. If the month-end
change was not run, or the user picks a date in an older period, the posting is refused.

## Resolution steps
1. Check the posting date the user entered. Ask them to use a date in one of the two
   periods named in the message, if that matches when the movement really happened.
2. If the current calendar month is not among the allowed periods, the period was not
   moved forward. Check the current period with MMRV.
3. Escalate a missing period change to the materials-management team, who run MMPV.
4. Postings into an older closed period need Finance approval and are handled by
   Finance, not the helpdesk.

cited.title: VPN connected but internal sites do not open
cited.text:
VPN connected but internal sites do not open (VPN connectivity)
## Symptom
The VPN client says it is connected, but internal websites, file shares and SAP do not
open. Public websites still work.

## Cause
The VPN tunnel is up but the laptop is not using the internal DNS servers pushed by the
VPN, or a home router uses the same private address range as an internal network, so
traffic for that range never enters the tunnel.

## Resolution steps
1. Ask the user to try an internal resource by IP address. If the IP works but the name
   does not, it is a DNS problem.
2. Run `ipconfig /all` and check that the VPN adapter lists the internal DNS servers.
3. Disconnect and reconnect the VPN; if DNS is still wrong, reinstall the VPN profile from
   the software centre.
4. If even IP addresses fail, compare the home network's address range with the internal
   ranges (for example both using 192.168.1.x). Ask the user to restart the home router
   or test from a hotspot, and report the overlap to network engineering.

cited.title: Office Wi-Fi keeps dropping
cited.text:
Office Wi-Fi keeps dropping (Wireless access)
## Symptom
A laptop repeatedly disconnects from the office Wi-Fi, especially after being idle or
when the user moves between meeting rooms.

## Cause
Most often the adapter's power saving turns the radio down when idle, or the laptop holds
on to a distant access point. When many users in one area drop at once, an access point
or the wireless controller is at fault.

## Resolution steps
1. Ask whether colleagues in the same area are affected. If yes, record the location and
   escalate it as an access point problem.
2. Note the network name and the access point the laptop was last connected to, from the
   connection details.
3. Forget the network and reconnect to clear a stale saved profile.
4. Set the adapter's power management so Windows cannot turn it off to save power, and
   update the wireless driver from the software centre.

## Warnings
Do not tell users to connect to the guest network instead; it has no access to internal
systems.

cited.title: A query has become slow
cited.text:
A query has become slow (Query performance and indexes)
## Symptom
A report or application feature that used to be fast is now slow, gradually or suddenly
after a release or data growth.

## Cause
The query plan changed: a sequential scan over a large table instead of an index scan,
because an index is missing or table statistics are out of date. Sometimes the query does
far more work than needed.

## Resolution steps
1. Get the exact query from the application log or `pg_stat_statements`.
2. Run `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` on it (on a replica or test copy if it changes data).
3. Look for a sequential scan on a large table where an index scan is expected.
4. If the index exists but is not used, refresh statistics with `ANALYZE` on the table.
5. If an index is missing or the query is inefficient, send the plan to the owning team.

## Warnings
Do not create indexes on production tables without the DBA team; building them can lock
the table.

cited.title: Certificate errors in a desktop tool on the office network
cited.text:
Certificate errors in a desktop tool on the office network (Firewall and proxy)
## Symptom
A developer tool, command-line client or desktop app fails with an SSL or certificate
error ("unable to get local issuer certificate", "self-signed certificate in chain") on
the office network, but works at home.

## Cause
The web proxy inspects encrypted traffic and re-signs it with the company's root
certificate. Browsers trust that certificate, but some tools use their own certificate
store and do not.

## Resolution steps
1. Confirm the error appears only on the office network or VPN.
2. Point the tool at the company root certificate, which is published on the intranet
   (most tools have a setting or environment variable for a CA bundle).
3. If the tool cannot be configured, raise a request for an inspection bypass for that
   domain, with the business reason.

## Warnings
Never turn off certificate verification in the tool; it removes protection against
real interception.

Index causing query errors

Our database queries return incorrect results, blocking project progress. Logs show index errors after recent crashes and power outages.

claims.claim: Run the query again with index scans disabled: `SET enable_indexscan = off

cited.title: Index returns wrong results
cited.text:
Index returns wrong results (Query performance and indexes)
## Symptom
Queries return inconsistent or clearly wrong results, or the log shows index errors.

## Cause
The index is corrupted, usually after a crash, power loss or a storage fault during a write.

## Resolution steps
1. Run the query again with index scans disabled for the session
   (`SET enable_indexscan = off; SET enable_bitmapscan = off;`). If the results differ, the
   index is at fault.
2. Rebuild it with `REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY` so the table stays usable.
3. Find out why it happened: check the logs for crashes or storage errors.
4. If corruption comes back on the same storage, escalate to the storage team.

## Warnings
A plain `REINDEX` locks the table; use the concurrent form, or schedule a quiet window.

Schema migration failed

The migration stopped. Not sure what worked. Many reports are stuck. Need to fix soon. Also, emails aren't getting through today.

claims.claim: Check the version table (alembic_version) to see what the tool recorded.

cited.title: Schema migration failed halfway
cited.text:
Schema migration failed halfway (Access requests and schema changes)
## Symptom
A schema migration failed during deployment, and it is unclear which changes were applied.

## Cause
Migrations that are not run in one transaction (for example with `CREATE INDEX
CONCURRENTLY`) can stop halfway. The migration tool's version table may not match what
was really applied.

## Resolution steps
1. Check the version table (for example `alembic_version`) to see what the tool recorded.
2. Compare the actual schema with what the migration should produce.
3. Finish or undo the partial change by hand so the schema matches one known version.
4. Then mark the version or rerun the migration, and record what was done in the ticket.

## Warnings
Never rerun a failed migration before you know which statements already applied.

cited.title: Schema change hangs and blocks the whole table
cited.text:
Schema change hangs and blocks the whole table (Locks and deadlocks)
## Symptom
An `ALTER TABLE` during a deployment hangs, and soon all queries on that table are blocked
too, causing an application outage.

## Cause
`ALTER TABLE` needs an exclusive lock. It waits behind any running transaction on the
table, and every new query then queues behind the waiting `ALTER TABLE`.

## Resolution steps
1. Cancel the waiting `ALTER TABLE` session to release the queue at once.
2. Find the long-running transaction it was waiting for.
3. Rerun the migration in a quiet window with a short `lock_timeout` (for example a few
   seconds), so it gives up instead of blocking everyone.
4. Retry the migration if it times out, rather than letting it wait.

## Warnings
Never run schema changes on busy tables without a lock timeout.

cited.title: Background job not starting or stuck
cited.text:
Background job not starting or stuck (Batch jobs and IDocs)
## Symptom
A background job in SM37 stays "Released" or "Ready" and never becomes "Active", or it
stays "Active" for much longer than usual.

## Cause
"Released" means the job is waiting for its start condition (date, time or event).
"Ready" means the start condition is met but no background work process is free. A long
"Active" job is usually waiting on a database lock or processing far more data than usual.

claims.claim: If the status is 'Released', verify the start condition (date, time or event).

## Cause

cited.title: Background job not starting or stuck
cited.text:
Background job not starting or stuck (Batch jobs and IDocs)
## Resolution steps
1. Open the job in SM37 and note its status and planned start.
2. If "Released", check the start condition: a future start time or an event that has not
   been raised yet is normal.
3. If "Ready", check in SM50 whether all background work processes are busy. The job
   starts when one frees up. Report it to Basis if this persists.
4. If "Active" for too long, open the job log in SM37 and note the last step; check SM12
   for locks held by the job's user.
5. A job with no log progress for 30 minutes or more is cancelled by Basis, not the user.

## Warnings
Do not cancel and reschedule a running job without checking what it was posting; a
half-finished posting run can leave inconsistent documents.

cited.title: Wi-Fi access for a visitor
cited.text:
Wi-Fi access for a visitor (Wireless access)
## Symptom
An employee asks for internet access for a visitor, contractor or vendor who is on site.

## Cause
Visitors may not join the corporate network. Guest access is a separate, isolated network
with time-limited credentials sponsored by an employee.

## Resolution steps
1. Confirm the request comes from an employee who sponsors the guest. Visitors cannot
   request access for themselves.
2. Create a guest credential or day pass in the guest portal, with an expiry that matches
   the visit. Never issue a credential without an expiry.
3. Record the sponsor and the visit dates in the ticket for audit.
4. If the visitor needs internal systems, explain that this is a separate access request
   with its own approval. Never put a visitor on the corporate network.

## Warnings
Guest Wi-Fi is deliberately bandwidth-limited and isolated; "slow" guest Wi-Fi is not a
fault to fix.

Certificate errors in tool

Developer tool fails with SSL error at work. Works fine at home without issues. Error message: 'unable to get local issuer certificate'. Same tool works fine on home network. Can you check if there's an update for the tool's certificate store?

claims.claim: Confirm the error appears only on the office network or VPN.

cited.title: Certificate errors in a desktop tool on the office network
cited.text:
Certificate errors in a desktop tool on the office network (Firewall and proxy)
## Symptom
A developer tool, command-line client or desktop app fails with an SSL or certificate
error ("unable to get local issuer certificate", "self-signed certificate in chain") on
the office network, but works at home.

## Cause
The web proxy inspects encrypted traffic and re-signs it with the company's root
certificate. Browsers trust that certificate, but some tools use their own certificate
store and do not.

## Resolution steps
1. Confirm the error appears only on the office network or VPN.
2. Point the tool at the company root certificate, which is published on the intranet
   (most tools have a setting or environment variable for a CA bundle).
3. If the tool cannot be configured, raise a request for an inspection bypass for that
   domain, with the business reason.

## Warnings
Never turn off certificate verification in the tool; it removes protection against
real interception.

Cannot write to database

I'm encountering an erroor stating 'cannot execute INSERT in a read-only transaction' when trying to save data. This seems to happen aftter a failover, as the application still points to the old primary server. Could you please assist in resolving this issue quickly?

claims.claim: Check the database logs for the exact transaction that is failing.

cited.title: Transaction fails with deadlock detected
cited.text:
Transaction fails with deadlock detected (Locks and deadlocks)
## Symptom
A transaction fails with "deadlock detected" and is rolled back, sometimes only under load.

## Cause
Two transactions lock the same rows in opposite order, each waiting for the other.
PostgreSQL detects this and cancels one of them. The data is safe; the cancelled
transaction must be retried.

## Resolution steps
1. Get the deadlock details from the database log: it shows both statements and the locks
   involved.
2. Look for code paths that update the same tables in a different order.
3. Ask the owning team to lock rows in a consistent order (for example by primary key) and
   to retry transactions that fail with a deadlock.
4. If a batch job collides with user traffic, move it to a quieter time or split it into
   smaller transactions.

## Warnings
A deadlock is not data corruption; do not restore backups because of one.

cited.title: Request for access to a database
cited.text:
Request for access to a database (Access requests and schema changes)
## Symptom
A developer or a service asks for read or write access to a database, schema or table.

## Cause
Access is granted per role. A new project or service often needs access that nobody has
requested yet.

## Resolution steps
1. Confirm the exact scope (table, schema or database) and whether read-only or read-write.
2. Get the manager's approval and the business reason.
3. Grant the narrowest existing role that fits, for example the schema's read-only role.
   For a service, create a dedicated role for that service.
4. Record who, what, why and when in the ticket, and an end date for temporary access.

## Warnings
Never add a person to the database owner or superuser role to grant access.

cited.text:

## Symptom
An analyst asks to connect a reporting or BI tool directly to a production database.

## Cause
Heavy reporting queries on the primary database slow down the applications that use it.
Reporting is served from a read replica with a read-only role.

## Resolution steps
1. Confirm which data the analyst needs and the manager's approval.
2. Grant the reporting read-only role on the read replica, not on the primary.
3. Give the analyst the replica's connection details and explain that data may lag a few
   seconds.
4. For personal data, check with the data protection officer before granting access.

## Warnings
Reporting tools never connect to the primary database.

cited.title: Application runs out of database connections
cited.text:
Application runs out of database connections (Connections and pools)
## Symptom
Application logs show "connection pool exhausted", "sorry, too many clients already", or
requests waiting for a database connection, while the database server is up.

## Cause
Either the database reached `max_connections`, or the application's pool is full because
code paths take connections and never return them (a leak), often after an unhandled
error. Sessions left "idle in transaction" also hold connection slots.

## Resolution steps
1. Compare the number of connections in `pg_stat_activity` with `SHOW max_connections`.
2. Group the sessions by application and state; many "idle in transaction" sessions from
   one application point to that application.
3. Check whether the errors started after a deployment; a new code path that does not
   close its connection is the usual cause.
4. As a stop-gap, restart the affected application instance to release leaked connections.
5. Send the findings to the owning team to fix the leak or pool settings.

## Warnings
Raising `max_connections` hides a leak and costs memory on the server; fix the leak first.

## Symptom
Application logs show "connection pool exhausted", "sorry, too many clients already", or
requests waiting for a database connection, while the database server is up.

## Cause
Either the database reached `max_connections`, or the application's pool is full because
code paths take connections and never return them (a leak), often after an unhandled
error. Sessions left "idle in transaction" also hold connection slots.

## Resolution steps
1. Compare the number of connections in `pg_stat_activity` with `SHOW max_connections`.
2. Group the sessions by application and state; many "idle in transaction" sessions from
   one application point to that application.
3. Check whether the errors started after a deployment; a new code path that does not
   close its connection is the usual cause.
4. As a stop-gap, restart the affected application instance to release leaked connections.
5. Send the findings to the owning team to fix the leak or pool settings.

## Warnings
Raising `max_connections` hides a leak and costs memory on the server; fix the leak first.
